You will also mentor trainers, maintain quality standards, and drive consistent task delivery.

What you'll do:
  • Lead and mentor a pod of technical trainers, ensuring consistent quality, productivity, and timely delivery of chemical engineering tasks.
  • Review engineering tasks end to end, including problem statements, reaction kinetics, thermodynamic and property data, process flowsheets, computational environments, reference solutions, and automated tests.
  • Validate tasks involving reaction engineering, thermodynamics, phase equilibria, transport phenomena, separation processes, process simulation, process control, optimization, combustion, and electrochemical engineering.
  • Ensure tasks reflect realistic chemical engineering workflows and require meaningful multi-step technical reasoning.
  • Verify engineering correctness across mass and energy balances, thermodynamic consistency, property data, unit handling, and numerical convergence.
  • Validate computational models, stiff ODE/DAE solvers, solver tolerances, initial conditions, and simulation results to ensure reproducibility and technical accuracy.
  • Review automated graders to ensure they evaluate meaningful engineering outputs such as conversion, yield, selectivity, purity, energy consumption, and process constraint satisfaction.
  • Identify technical inaccuracies, unrealistic assumptions, incorrect tolerances, and opportunities to bypass engineering calculations or simulations.
  • Provide clear, actionable technical feedback, track revisions, and ensure quality issues are resolved before task approval.
  • Onboard trainers, allocate work, monitor quality and throughput, escalate blockers, and maintain technical documentation and best practices.

What we're looking for:
  • Ph.D., postdoctoral experience, or equivalent advanced technical experience in Chemical Engineering.
  • Strong programming skills in Python, Julia, C/C++, or MATLAB/Octave, with proficiency in Linux environments.
  • Hands-on expertise in at least one major area: process modeling, reaction kinetics, thermodynamic modeling, process simulation, or optimization.
  • Strong understanding of chemical engineering fundamentals, numerical methods, computational modeling, and technical validation.
  • Experience reviewing complex technical work, chemical process simulations, computational models, or research outputs.
  • Ability to evaluate mass and energy balances, thermodynamic assumptions, numerical accuracy, solver convergence, and the reliability of computational results.
  • Strong analytical judgment with the ability to identify technical errors, edge cases, and flawed engineering assumptions.
  • Experience mentoring, reviewing, or leading small technical teams.
  • Excellent written communication skills for providing precise technical feedback and documenting quality standards.

Nice to have:
  • Experience with chemical engineering simulation and computational tools such as Cantera, CoolProp, Pyomo, IDAES, DWSIM, CasADi, or OpenFOAM.

title: Wi-Fi Engineer, Hardware Reliability (Starlink)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

WI-FI ENGINEER, HARDWARE RELIABILITY (STARLINK)

SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and millions of consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.

As an RF/Wi-Fi Engineer on the Starlink Reliability team, you will perform telemetry and log analysis as well as hands-on debugging to drive to root cause and corrective action of failed hardware. You will build and maintain tools and custom software to assess the performance and reliability of Starlink customer hardware (dishes, routers, power supplies, etc.) and support internal betas and product launches.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Perform telemetry and log analysis as well as hands-on debugging to drive to root cause and corrective action of failed phased-array, Wi-Fi, and power supply PCBAs
  • Build and maintain critical tools and custom software to objectively assess the performance and reliability of Starlink customer hardware
  • Run internal betas and product launches to identify and resolve any design issues in the hardware or software of new products ahead of their public launch
  • Build relationships and collaborate across disciplines including engineering, production, test, inventory, quality, supply chain, and customer experience to drive positive business outcomes
  • Consistently contribute effort, leadership, and creative thinking to solving complex problems in a collaborative fashion and under tight deadlines

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, RF engineering, computer engineering, computer science, mathematics, or other STEM discipline
  • 1+ years of experience working with digital or mixed-signal designs, using oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, power supplies, and/or soldering equipment (includes internships and school projects)
  • 1+ years of experience with networking technologies including ethernet protocols and Wi-Fi standards
  • 1+ years of experience with data analysis in Python/R

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 1+ years experience in consumer electronics or similar industry
  • Experience troubleshooting electronics hardware
  • Proficiency at understanding PCB schematics and layout tools
  • Experience with engineering projects in any one or more of the following areas: CPU/FPGA/ASIC circuit boards, Linux, high-speed interfaces, memories, and/or low-power platforms
  • Experience with basic principles of antenna theory, RF antennas, and communication systems
  • Experience troubleshooting RF communication systems including Wi-Fi
  • Understanding of service provider and home network technologies including but not limited to:
    • Connectivity (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, WDM, IPv4, and IPv6)
    • Internet services (DNS, DHCP, NTP, UPnP, NAT, etc.)
    • Knowledge and troubleshooting of most common consumer devices (NAS, IoT, smart devices, etc.)
  • Experience working within complex software-defined networking (SDN) and/or network function virtualization (NFV) environments
  • 1+ years of experience with SQL
  • Strong coding skills: clean, efficient, and well-documented code with a foundation in software design principles
  • Experience in a technical operational role under the pressure of a live service or high-volume production environment (e.g., consumer goods, automotive)
  • Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment that includes working with changing needs and requirements
  • Self-motivated independent learner with strong multi-tasking, organizational, communication, and documentation skills
  • Ability to identify customer needs, gather requirements, and execute independently

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • This position is based in Bastrop, TX (near Austin) and requires being on-site; hybrid or remote work not considered
  • Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed
  • Must be willing to travel up to 10% for work

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Microscopy Officer
description:
• Institute for Molecular Bioscience
  • Full-time fixed-term position for up to 2 years
  • Full-time equivalent base salary will be in the range $97,268.85 - $104,348.98 + 17% super (HEW Level 6)
  • Based at our St Lucia Campus

About This Opportunity

As Microscopy Officer, you will be at the heart of discovery, partnering with the Microscopy Platform Manager to deliver world‑class optical, fluorescence and confocal microscopy services at IMB. Working alongside passionate researchers and state‑of‑the‑art infrastructure, you will help turn complex biological questions into clear, high‑impact insights. Your contribution will directly enable exceptional research outcomes across the Institute, University and external partners, while fostering a vibrant culture of shared learning, operational excellence and scientific curiosity aligned to UQ’s purpose of creating change together.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Coordinating and delivering individual and group training in microscope operation, image acquisition, visualisation software and image analysis for biological research.
  • Maintaining, cleaning and calibrating microscopy instrumentation to factory specifications, and supporting the day-to-day operation of the imaging platform.
  • Providing responsive, helpdesk style troubleshooting for minor equipment and software issues, and escalating complex matters as required.
  • Managing platform assets and records, including stocktakes, consumables ordering, user training logs, work records and associated charges.
  • Contributing to the continuous improvement of facility procedures, documentation, and user support resources.
  • Supporting the safe and effective operation of the imaging platform in accordance with institutional policies and laboratory standards.


About You

You will bring a strong technical foundation, a service-oriented mindset and a genuine enthusiasm for supporting others to do their best science. You will also demonstrate:

  • A degree in a biological or biomedical discipline, or an equivalent combination of relevant experience and education or training.
  • Demonstrated experience operating and maintaining optical microscopes, including fluorescence and confocal systems, in a research setting.
  • Practical laboratory experience relevant to microscopy, such as histology techniques including fixation, embedding, sectioning and staining or immunofluorescence sample preparation and labelling.
  • Proven expertise in applying advanced biomedical or life science microscopy techniques to analyse structure, morphology and function.
  • Well-developed organisational, interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively, and to prepare professional documentation on complex matters.
  • Experience delivering training or teaching users in microscope and equipment operation, or the capability and confidence to develop these skills.
  • Desirable experience with widefield and confocal microscope systems as well as image processing and quantification methods for multi-dimensional datasets.
  • Familiarity with Windows-based administrative systems, scientific image analysis software, scripting, or programming languages relevant to image acquisition and analysis (e.g., Python, ImageJ/Fiji macros, MATLAB).

About UQ

As part of the UQ community, you’ll have the opportunity to work alongside the brightest minds, who have joined us from all over the world, working together to create a better world. Join a community where excellence is at the core of our culture, contributions are valued and a range of benefits and rewards are available.

Enjoy up to 26 weeks paid parental and primary care leave, 17% super, 17.5% leave loading, flexible and hybrid working options, health and wellbeing programs, a heavily discounted Study for Staff program, on‑campus childcare, affordable parking, and salary packaging.

Interested?

For more information about this opportunity, please contact Dr Nicholas Condon at n.condon@uq.edu.au.

For application inquiries, please reach out to the Talent Acquisition team at talent@uq.edu.au, stating the job reference number (below) in the subject line.

When you apply, please ensure you upload a resume and cover letter summarising how your background aligns to the ‘About You’ section. Please note that applications received via email will not be accepted.

Other Information

Pre-employment checks may include: verification of the right to work in Australia. This may also include checks relating to gender-based violence matters or other integrity and conduct requirements.

You must maintain unrestricted work rights in Australia for the duration of this appointment to apply. Employer sponsored work rights are not available for this appointment.

description:
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Acts as the Affiliate’s main contact point for pharmacovigilance PV matters with the National Regulatory Agency and AbbVie Global Patient Safety (GPS).

Periodic Safety Reporting:

  • Partners with the Regional PV Team in GPS to support Periodic and Aggregate Reports to the Regulatory Agencies, Ethics Committees and Investigators, in compliance with corporate PV procedures and with local and regional PV regulations as required.
  • Cooperation with local RA team to prepare License renewal PSUR and local Annex to support application submission to HA.

Audits and Inspections:

  • Act as the key contact for Affiliate PV audits and Regulatory Authority PV inspections.
  • Support and ensure that any audit/inspection responses/corrective actions are completed according to the schedule.
  • Support to collaborate with the GPS Regional PV Team audits as well as of affiliate service providers and third parties.

Risk Management:

  • Ensure local risk management activities in alignment with local regulations.
  • Coordinates the receipt and distribution of Risk Management Plans (RMPs), Core Implementation Strategy (CIS) and additional risk minimization measures (aRMM) to relevant affiliate stakeholders.
  • Understand the RMP to obtain information on the risk/benefit profile of products.
  • Liaises with the affiliate stakeholders and the Office of Risk Management and where applicable, seek involvement of relevant global stakeholders during development or revision of the local RMP or RMP Annex (if applicable), Local Implementation Plan (LIP) & local or country-specific aRMM.
  • Performs the assessment and implementation of the CIS and accompanying aRMM, when applicable.

Safety Monitoring and Evidence Generation:

  • Maintains an overview of medicinal product safety profiles and any emerging safety concerns for company products marketed within the relevant jurisdiction, and maintains awareness of conditions or obligations adopted as part of the marketing authorizations, commitments relating to safety or the safe use of the products and of post-authorization safety studies requested by a regulatory agency.
  • Understands and monitors incoming local safety data and communicate changes or potential concerns to the GPS Product Safety Team Lead and the EU QPPV (for products marketed in the EEA) for evaluation.
  • Through monitoring of safety data, the ASR back up ensures that robust evidence is generated to inform risk management, regulatory submissions, and product safety profiles.
  • Reviews summary reports of local research-related activities and communicates any safety insights/findings with Medical Teams and GPS.
  • As a member of product safety communication and education initiatives for local cross-functional teams on major PV topics and on local data sources.

Quality Management System:

  • Partners with the Regional PV Teams to:
    • Ensure Affiliate PV System procedure(s) aligns with corporate PV procedures and complies with local and regional PV regulations.
    • Manage any non-conformity and/or planned departures from corporate and/or local PV procedures according to the global issue and exception management process and ensure any corrective/preventive actions are completed according to the schedule.
    • Support oversight of the PV training plan and ensure training compliance of local PV personnel and other affiliate personnel with Corporate and Local PV training requirements.

Launch Readiness:

  • Sets a solid local safety and PV strategy incorporating proactive PV contributions to ensure a successful product or indication launch at the affiliate.
  • Acts as key safety advisor for affiliate cross-functional partners on safety topics.

title: Treatment Supervisor
description:
About Veolia

Veolia Australia & New Zealand is the only global company to provide a full range of environmental services in the fields of water, waste management and energy solutions. With the global expertise gained from serving the environment for more than 170 years.

The Opportunity

Veolia Water New Zealand is seeking an experienced Treatment Supervisor to oversee the operation and performance of wastewater treatment plants across the district.

Reporting to the Treatment Manager, you will lead the Wastewater Treatment Team, support operational and maintenance activities, monitor compliance, and drive continuous improvement across treatment processes and service delivery.

This is an important leadership role for a confident and technically capable professional who is committed to safety, environmental performance, operational excellence and maintaining strong client relationships.

What's on offer

  • Competitive salary

  • Full time permanent role

  • A great team focused working environment

  • Opportunities for professional growth and development

  • Stable employment with a reputable, world leading, 3 waters Network focused organisation

  • Meaningful work that contributes to the well-being of our community and keeps the cogs of society turning.

  • Employee assistance programs (EAP) through assure which covers mental health, nutrition, financial, legal, coaching and career transition support

What you'll be responsible for

You will be responsible for:

  • Providing day-to-day leadership, guidance and support to the Wastewater Treatment Team
  • Prioritising work, supporting performance management and contributing to staff development plans
  • Monitoring and reporting on wastewater treatment performance, including resource consent compliance, sampling requirements and contractual KPIs
  • Identifying and implementing corrective actions to prevent or address non-compliance
  • Advising on the operation and maintenance of wastewater treatment processes and systems
  • Supporting projects that improve and optimise treatment plant performance
  • Coordinating operational and contract reporting for Veolia management and Central Hawke’s Bay District Council
  • Implementing changes to consent requirements and operational procedures
  • Supporting compliance events, consent breach responses and environmental improvement programmes
  • Operating the district-wide SCADA system to monitor and control remote sites and alarm systems
  • Ensuring asset information is accurately captured and maintained in AssetFinda
  • Supporting Health and Safety, Quality Assurance and Environmental Management Systems
  • Participating in a supervisory-level on-call roster
  • Escalating risks and providing early warnings where required
  • Building and maintaining positive relationships with clients, customers and team members

What you'll need to be successful

You will bring:

  • A New Zealand Certificate in Wastewater Treatment, relevant industry qualification, or equivalent experience
  • Experience in wastewater treatment operations, maintenance or a related process industry
  • An understanding of wastewater treatment technologies, processes and operational requirements
  • Knowledge of resource consents and the importance of compliance
  • Proven leadership and team coordination skills
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making abilities
  • Experience preparing clear and concise reports
  • Strong communication and relationship management skills
  • The ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively as part of a team
  • A strong understanding of SCADA systems
  • Sound computer skills, including Microsoft Office
  • A current, valid driver’s licence
  • The flexibility and willingness to work outside normal hours when required

You will be a confident and practical leader who can make sound decisions under pressure, manage competing priorities and maintain a strong focus on safety, quality and environmental outcomes.

Why Veolia?

At Veolia Australia and New Zealand, you’ll join a team of over 6500 passionate innovators... and good humans. Our environmental solutions help customers preserve and renew our natural resources, creating a better future for our planet. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to build your career, and resource the world.

If you can tick most of the boxes and are keen to contribute to Veolia’s ecological transformation, then hit the apply button now!

THIS STEP IS IMPORTANT

To apply for this vacancy you MUST be a New Zealand citizen, resident, or have already secured the right to work in New Zealand and therefore hold a valid visa.

Fairness, Diversity & Inclusion

At Veolia we value diversity, equality and inclusion, we are committed to providing working environments where everyone is included and treated fairly and with respect. We welcome applications from Maori and Pasifika, Veterans, people with disability, mature age and early careers, members of the LGBTI+ community and people from all cultural backgrounds.

title: Dir-Food & Beverage-A
description:
JOB SUMMARY

Functions as the strategic business leader of the property’s food and beverage/culinary operation, including Restaurants/Bars, Room Service and Banquets/Catering, where applicable. Position oversees the development and implementation of departmental strategies and ensures implementation of the brand service strategy and brand initiatives. The position ensures the food and beverage/culinary operation meets the brand’s target customer needs, ensures employee satisfaction, and focuses on growing revenues and maximizing the financial performance of the department. Develops and implements property-wide strategies that deliver products and services to meet or exceed the needs and expectations of the brand’s target customer and property employees and provides a return on investment.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or GED; 6 years experience in the food and beverage, culinary, event management, or related professional area.

OR

• 2-year degree from an accredited university in Food Service Management, Hotel and Restaurant Management, Hospitality, Business Administration, or related major; 4 years experience in the food and beverage, culinary, event management, or related professional area.

Skills and Knowledge

• Luxury Experience – Capable to execute luxury F&B experience throughout the hotel food & Beverage operation, deeply personalized and flawless orchestration of execution, setting and anticipation

• Concept Development: Able to develop Food & Beverages concepts for outlets, develop teams to execute star rated operational standards alongside the culinary team

. Customer and Personal Service - Knowledge of principles and processes for providing customer and personal services. This includes customer needs assessment, meeting quality standards for services, and evaluation of customer satisfaction.

• Management of Financial Resources - Determining how money will be spent to get the work done, and accounting for these expenditures.

• Administration and Management - Knowledge of business and management principles involved in strategic planning, resource allocation, human resources modeling, leadership technique, production methods, and coordination of people and resources.

• Applied Business Knowledge - Understanding market dynamics, enterprise level objectives and important aspects of the company’s business to accurately diagnose strengths and weaknesses, anticipate opportunities and risks, identify issues, and develop strategies and plans. Aligning individual and team actions with strategies and plans to drive business results.

• Management of Material Resources - Obtaining and seeing to the appropriate use of equipment, facilities, and materials needed to do certain work.

CORE WORK ACTIVITIES

Developing and Maintaining Food and Beverage/Culinary Goals

• Sets expectations and holds food and beverage leadership team accountable for demonstrating desired service behaviors.

• Reviews financial reports and statements to determine how Food and Beverage is performing against budget.

• Makes recommendations for CAPEX funding of food and beverage equipment and renovations in accordance with brand business strategy.

• Works with food and beverage leadership team to determine areas of concern and develops strategies to improve the department’s financial performance.

• Establishes challenging, realistic and obtainable goals to guide operation and performance.

• Strives to improve service performance.

Developing and Maintaining Budgets

• Develops and manages Food and Beverage budget.

• Monitors the department’s actual and projected sales to ensure revenue goals are met or exceeded and opportunities are identified and addressed.

• Ensures cash control and liquor control policies are in place in food & beverage areas and followed by all related employees.

• Focuses on maintaining profit margins without compromising guest or employee satisfaction.

Leading Food and Beverage/Culinary Team

• Utilizes interpersonal and communication skills to lead, influence, and encourage others; advocates sound financial/business decision making; demonstrates honesty/integrity; leads by example.

• Encourages and builds mutual trust, respect, and cooperation among team members.

• Achieves and exceeds goals including performance goals, budget goals, team goals, etc.

• Serves as a role model to demonstrate appropriate behaviors.

• Develops means to improve profit, including estimating cost and benefit, exploring new business opportunities, etc.

• Identifies opportunities to increase profits and create value by challenging existing processes, encouraging innovation and driving necessary change.

• Ensures that regular, on-going communication occurs in all areas of food and beverage (e.g., pre-meal briefings, staff meetings, culinary team).

• Establishes and maintains open, collaborative relationships with direct reports and entire food & beverage team. Ensures direct reports do the same for their team.

• Develops a food and beverage operating strategy that is aligned with the brand’s business strategy and leads its execution.

• Identifies the developmental needs of others and coaches, mentors, or otherwise helps others to improve their knowledge or skills.

• Stays aware of market trends and introduces new food and beverage products to meet or exceed customer expectations, generate increased revenue and ensure a competitive position in the market.

Ensuring Exceptional Customer Service

• Provides services that are above and beyond for customer satisfaction and retention.

• Improves service by communicating and assisting individuals to understand guest needs, providing guidance, feedback, and individual coaching when needed.

• Reviews findings from comment cards and guest satisfaction results with F& B team and ensures appropriate corrective action is taken.

• Reviews comment cards, guest satisfaction results and other data to identify areas of improvement.

• Empowers employees to provide excellent guest service.

• Estimates cost and benefit ratio, maintaining balance between profit and service satisfaction.

• Shares plans to take corrective action based on comment cards and guest satisfaction results with property leadership.

Managing and Conducting Human Resource Activities

• Provides guidance and direction to subordinates, including setting performance standards and monitoring performance.

• Coaches and supports food & beverage leadership team to effectively manage wages, food & beverage cost and controllable expenses (e.g., restaurant supplies, uniforms, etc.).

• Hires food & beverage leadership team members who demonstrate strong functional expertise, creativity and entrepreneurial leadership to meet the business needs of the operation.

• Sets goals and expectations for direct reports using the performance review process and holds staff accountable for successful performance.

• Ensures that expectations and objectives are clearly communicated to subordinates; subordinates are also open to raise questions and/or concerns.

• Brings issues to the attention of Human Resources as necessary.

• Ensures employees are treated fairly and equitably.

• Coaches team by providing specific feedback to improve performance.

Additional Responsibilities

• Informs and/or update the executives, the peers and the subordinates on relevant information in a timely manner.

• Provides information to supervisors, co-workers, and subordinates by telephone, in written form, e-mail, or in person.

• Analyzes information and evaluating results to choose the best solution and solve problems.

• Estimate food, liquor, wine, and other beverage consumption in order to anticipate amounts to be purchased or requisitioned.

• Order and purchase equipment and supplies.

title: Fashion PR & Events Internship (m/f/d)
description:
Fashion PR & Events Internship (m/f/d)

Put #DAMUR in the right inboxes, headlines, guest lists and cultural conversations.

Berlin · Primarily on-site · 3–6 months · Mandatory study internship

About the Role

#DAMUR is a Berlin-based high-end fashion label connecting gender-neutral fashion with music, nightlife, performance and contemporary culture.

You will turn collections, people and live moments into relevant stories for journalists, stylists, creators and cultural communities. You will support press outreach, sample coordination, guest-list communication and event visibility. This role focuses on PR and event communication; it does not include sponsorship sales.

A Professional Working Internship

This is a professional working internship—not a classroom, observation placement or beginner training programme.

We provide clear briefs, professional context, feedback and access to real projects. In return, you are expected to bring usable communication skills, think independently, take ownership and contribute to meaningful progress and results.

You do not need to know everything on your first day, but you must be resourceful, accountable and ready to learn through doing. We are looking for students who want to add value to the team—not wait for every step to be taught or repeatedly explained.

What You’ll Do

  • Research relevant journalists, publications, stylists, creators and cultural platforms
  • Maintain accurate press, stylist, creator and event contact lists
  • Develop story angles and draft press releases, invitations and tailored outreach
  • Coordinate samples, image requests, credits and press materials
  • Manage invitations, RSVPs, guest lists and event communication
  • Follow up professionally and move conversations forward without repeated reminders
  • Track replies, published coverage, links and relevant media results
  • Take responsibility for defined outreach cycles and support events on-site

You’re a Strong Fit If

  • You study PR, communication, journalism, fashion communication, media or a related subject
  • You write concise, confident and professional English
  • You can identify a relevant story—not only repeat information from a press release
  • You research beyond obvious contacts and understand why a pitch fits a specific publication
  • You take responsibility for defined tasks and can work without step-by-step supervision
  • You ask focused questions, act on feedback and communicate early when blocked
  • You are organised, diplomatic and comfortable following up
  • You care about accuracy, deadlines and results—not only completing assigned hours
  • PR, editorial, showroom, event, German or Mandarin experience is a plus

What You’ll Gain

  • Real responsibility within active fashion PR and event communication
  • Direct contact with media, stylists, creators and cultural platforms
  • Experience developing story angles and managing an outreach cycle
  • Direct professional feedback on the quality, relevance and impact of your communication
  • Portfolio-relevant writing where confidentiality and publication permissions allow

Practical Information

  • Location: Berlin, primarily on-site
  • Start: As soon as possible; the exact date is agreed with the selected candidate
  • Duration: 3–6 months
  • Eligibility: This must be a mandatory internship required by your university or a recognised study programme. Erasmus+ placements are welcome when they meet this condition
  • You must already have the right to complete an internship in Germany; we cannot provide employer visa sponsorship
  • Transport support: Your Berlin AB ticket or Deutschlandticket is fully covered
  • Studio benefits: Daily warm homemade lunch, La Marzocco espresso, snacks and drinks
  • Schedule: Occasional evening or weekend work may be needed for events; this will always be agreed in advance

How to Apply

Apply in English through Fashion United by clicking "Apply.”

Upload your CV in PDF format and one English writing or communication sample.

In the Motivation field, answer the following in a maximum of 300 words:

  1. Choose one #DAMUR story you would pitch, name one specific publication or cultural platform and explain why the story fits its audience.
  2. Tell us about one PR, communication or event task you were responsible for. What did you do, and what was the result?
  3. State your earliest possible start date, how long you can stay (3–6 months), and confirm that this is a mandatory study internship.

No formal cover letter is required. We want to understand how you think, communicate and respond to a brief—not read a generic letter about your background or what you hope to gain. Please answer all three questions directly.

title: Time Capture Team Lead
description:
The opportunity

We have an opportunity for an experienced Time Capture Lead to join our Energy and Utilities Support Services Hub on a 12 month fixed term contract, providing maternity leave cover.

In this leadership role, you will oversee a team of timesheet administrators responsible for workforce time capture and payroll support activities. You will ensure timesheet records are accurate, complete and submitted in line with critical payroll processing deadlines.

Working closely with Payroll Operations, Site Coordinators, supervisors and operational teams, you will provide strong governance across time capture processes, manage payroll related risks and support consistent practices across our operational sites.

What we’re looking for

You will be an organised and collaborative leader with experience across payroll administration, workforce time capture or payroll support. You will be comfortable working in a deadline driven operational environment where accuracy, communication and effective workload management are critical.

• Experience in payroll administration, workforce time capture or payroll support

• Previous experience supervising or coordinating a payroll or timesheet administration team

• Experience supporting payroll processes within an operational or project based environment

• Strong knowledge of workforce time capture and payroll input requirements

• Experience using workforce management systems such as WebTimes, Kronos or similar

• The ability to identify and resolve timesheet and payroll discrepancies

• Strong leadership and workload coordination capabilities

• Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills

• High attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities

What we offer

• Supportive and collaborative team environment
• Flexible working opportunities available
• Access to employee benefits and wellbeing programs
• Exposure to a large scale essential services business
• A culture focused on safety, inclusion and continuous improvement

About Energy & Utilities

Downer is a leading provider of integrated services in Australia and New Zealand. Through our Energy & Utilities business, we provide essential services that support our customers and communities.

title: Assistant Manager - Engineering - Fairmont Mumbai and Roswyn, A Morgans Originals Hotel
description:
Job Purpose

To ensure the safe placement, inspection, testing, and commissioning of all electrical systems in the hotel and plant room machinery, ensuring their smooth and efficient operation.

Prime Function

Oversee the installation, testing, and maintenance of electrical systems and plant room machinery, coordinating with relevant vendors and management to ensure that all systems are fully operational, safe, and compliant with standards.

Key Responsibilities

Understanding and Oversight of Electrical Systems

  • Thoroughly understand the High Tension (HT), Low Tension (LT), and LT to Distribution side Single Line Diagrams (SLD).
  • Actively participate in the installation, testing, and commissioning of transformers, LT panels, and bus duct systems.
  • Involves the testing and commissioning of each HT and LT breaker, ensuring all parameters meet the required standards.
  • Ensure that transformer testing results are satisfactory and report any issues promptly.

Generator and Plant Room Machinery Management

  • Inspect the mechanical and electrical fittings of generators, ensuring that load testing is performed jointly, and all parameters meet operational requirements.
  • Oversee the testing and commissioning of bus duct systems, verifying that all parameters adhere to established standards.
  • Take handover of chillers, pumps, and all plant room machinery, ensuring their technical parameters align with design specifications.

Operational Testing and Maintenance

  • Supervision of Maintenance:
    • Supervise the maintenance and repair of the hotel's interior and exterior, including guest rooms, common areas, and external facilities. Work with the Design and Construction team, engineers, and outside architects for renovations and other projects.
  • Regularly monitor the operation of all pumps and systems, ensuring they function according to design parameters.
  • Fully engaged in the testing and commissioning of all major plant machinery, ensuring that all parameters meet operational needs.
  • Conduct daily inspections of the plant room area, reporting progress and issues as they arise.
  • Routinely check each floor’s electrical work, ensuring quality and safety, and coordinate with electrical vendors to understand the cable routing and distribution panels.

Documentation and Record-Keeping

  • Take responsibility for the handover of all systems, ensuring that they are operational and that all relevant documentation, including drawings and technical readings, is properly recorded.
  • Create and maintain service trackers for each system, updating history cards regularly.
  • Feed daily technical readings into the HLP sheet and maintain utility and waste management records.

Shift Management and Reporting

  • Conduct daily inspections of plant rooms and equipment, managing energy and water use, and maintaining log sheets for shift activities.
  • Follow up on pending work, ensuring a smooth handover to the next shift.
  • Oversee the proper handover of tools and ensure logbooks are signed by senior managers and shift-in-charge personnel.
  • Ensure that all major breakdowns during shifts are resolved before shift change, continuing the shift if a reliever is unavailable.
  • Perform the rotational/ specific shifts as and when the operational requirements and DOE allocations.
  • Emergency Response:
    • Be prepared to respond to any emergency situations during shifts, ensuring the safety and security of guests, staff, and property.

Vendor Coordination and Support

  • Provide support to vendors during their visits to the hotel, maintaining control over all contracted work according to established policies and procedures.
  • Manage the logbook of received materials, maintain the stores, and oversee the procurement process, raising purchase requests (PR) as needed.

Safety and Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with safety protocols, including confined spaces permits, hot work permits, risk assessments, and working at heights permits.
  • Oversee the safe operation of cooling towers and freshwater tanks, maintaining appropriate water levels.
  • Ensure all utilities have updated history cards and that all electrical safety procedures, including lockout/tagout, are followed.
  • Coordinate HSE Audits, FSSAI compliance, and thermography assessments and ensure that the property score is excellent.

Planned Preventive Maintenance

  • All the machine & equipment should undergo periodic preventive maintenance as per schedule approved by DOE or Hotel Managenment aligning with the brand standard.
  • All necessary licenses need to be reviewed and if required to be renewed.
  • All necessary local compliance to be reviewed and followed as per requirement.

Public Area and Plant Room Operations

  • Oversee the testing and commissioning of electrical systems in public areas.
  • Ensure the smooth operation of the sewage treatment plant (STP) and the cleanliness of areas like the transformer room, diesel generator (DG) room, RMU, and HT & LT panels.
  • Ensure proper handover of mobile and computer systems to the next shift and manage the DND card process during shifts.

Team Management

Staffing & Recruitment:

  • Plan for future staffing needs, interview, select, and recruit team members. Identify and develop team members with potential and provide mentorship and training for career advancement.

Performance Management:

  • Conduct regular performance reviews, monitor team members’ appearance, attitude, and professionalism. Provide constructive feedback and guidance to ensure high standards are maintained.

Training & Development:

  • Develop and maintain staff training programs focused on skill development and meeting the changing needs of the business. Prepare weekly staff schedules in line with anticipated business needs and operating budgets.

Team Communication:

  • Conduct monthly departmental meetings to share information, obtain feedback, address operational issues, and maintain open lines of communication within the team.
  • Maintain team grooming, hygiene, and effective communication standards.
  • Resolve all shift-related complaints promptly, managing manpower efficiently and ensuring smooth operations across all areas.

Main Complexity/Critical issues in the Job

Be proficient and efficient in all aspects of area of expertise, and adopt pro-active approach to problem solving.

title: Student Financials Officer
description:
Overview:

RMIT Vietnam is looking for a Student Financials Officer for supporting the delivery of student financial processes across the student lifecycle at RMIT Vietnam.

Expected start date: at the earliest available opportunity


WHY JOIN RMIT VIETNAM?

At RMIT Vietnam, international exposure meets real-world impact through strong industry and government collaboration. Working at RMIT means building a meaningful career while creating impact in a high-performing environment.

Further insight into our mission, impact and global connections is available in the RMIT Vietnam Profile


WHAT WE OFFER

  • Competitive remuneration VND package for Vietnamese candidates.
  • 13th month Tet bonus
  • Private Health insurance for you and your family, plus Personal Accident Insurance
  • Generous annual leave, sick leave, volunteer leave and public holidays (Christmas and Tet Holidays)
  • Professional development and career advancement
  • Access to state-of-the-art facilities and resources
  • A vibrant and diverse campus life and more!


POSITION SUMMARY

The Student Financials Officer is responsible for supporting the delivery of student financial processes across the student lifecycle at RMIT Vietnam. The role supports the accurate and timely processing of student financial activities, including billing, refunds, and student insurance, in accordance with University policies and procedures. It contributes to the day-to-day operations of the student financials function, ensuring data accuracy, compliance, and effective service delivery. Working under the guidance of the Senior Coordinator, Student Financials, the position supports workflow coordination, maintains financial records, and responds to student and stakeholder enquiries to ensure a consistent and high-quality student experience.

Reporting Line

Reports to: Senior Coordinator, Student Financials

Key relationships:

  • Internal Relationships: Academic Registrar’s Group (ARG) teams; Student Financials team; Enrolments and Student Records teams; Finance and Accounting; Student Connect; ITS; Student and Education Portfolio (SEP) units.
  • Global / Cross-campus Relationships: Relevant RMIT global stakeholders, including Student Financials Governance team.
  • External Relationships: Students and relevant external stakeholders (e.g. authorities or providers related to student insurance processes).

Reporting lines may be adjusted in line with organisational changes.


Key Accountabilities Summary

  • Process student financial transactions and activities, including billing, refunds, and payment-related requests, in accordance with established procedures and timelines.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial data in relevant systems, ensuring data integrity, confidentiality, and compliance with policies.
  • Respond to enquiries from students and stakeholders regarding student financial matters, providing accurate information and escalating complex cases where required.
  • Review and validate financial data, including invoices and student account information, ensuring accuracy for reporting and compliance purposes.
  • Support the coordination of student medical insurance processes, ensuring timely and accurate administration in line with institutional and regulatory requirements.
  • Assist in the implementation and testing of system or process changes related to student financials under the guidance of senior staff.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders, including Finance, Student Connect, ITS, and other ARG teams, to support coordinated service delivery.
  • Maintain professional and equitable service standards, particularly when supporting students experiencing financial difficulty.
  • Support documentation and maintenance of financial processes and operational guidelines.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying operational issues and supporting enhancements to processes and systems.
  • Undertake other duties as required by the line manager.
  • Other duties commensurate with the scope of the role

Key Selection Criteria

  • A relevant tertiary qualification (Bachelor’s degree at minimum requirement) or an equivalent combination of relevant experience.
  • Demonstrated experience (typically 1–3 years) in financial administration, billing, or related processes, preferably within a higher education or service-oriented environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy in managing financial data and information.
  • Experience working with administrative or financial systems and databases.
  • Demonstrated ability to follow processes and ensure compliance with policies and procedures.
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to respond to enquiries and support a range of stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage tasks, prioritise work, and meet deadlines in a structured environment.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and relevant digital tools.
  • Demonstrated commitment to service quality, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
  • Ability to display appropriate behaviours in line with the position, RMIT Values and RMIT Leadership Model.

Read more details at Job Description

title: Projectleider EU-fondsen
description:
Dit ga je doen

“Ik draag bij aan een slagvaardige Europese Unie! Dagelijks zet ik mij in voor de ontwikkeling van Nederland en Europa. Ja, daar krijg ik energie van. Mijn job is veelzijdig, uitdagend en leerzaam. De projecten, werkzaamheden en organisaties die ik onderzoek zijn heel verschillend; de ene keer verdiep ik me in het Europese subsidiebeheer en de andere keer voer ik een staatssteun-analyse uit.” Ousama Abouyakob, Projectleider EU-audit

Alle lidstaten van de Europese Unie ontvangen geld van de Europese Commissie, dit geld is verdeeld over diverse fondsen. Voor Nederland is de Auditdienst Rijk de auditautoriteit die deze geldstromen controleert. Maak jij het verschil door mensen in jouw controleteam te verbinden en te coachen? En kies jij de meest kwalitatieve controle-aanpak? Lees dan verder over de functie van Projectleider EU-audits.

Als (deel)projectleider is het jouw taak om onder aansturing van de auditmanager samen met het team de Europese Commissie zekerheid te bieden op de volgende vlakken:
• Is het management control system van de uitvoeringsorganisaties (organisaties die belast zijn met het verstrekken van EU-gelden) adequaat?
• Zijn de gedeclareerde uitgaven van subsidieontvangers juist, doel- en rechtmatig?
• Geeft de jaarrekening van de uitvoeringsorganisaties een getrouw beeld?
• Zijn de uitvoeringsorganisaties in control?
Om deze zekerheid te bieden voer jij controles en onderzoeken uit bij de uitvoeringsorganisaties en subsidieontvangers. De controles en onderzoeken vormen een mix van financial audits, IT-audits, performance audits, operational- en compliance auditing.

In deze rol:
• Ben je verantwoordelijk voor de controle van projecten met een grote diversiteit aan thema’s.
• Ben je medeverantwoordelijk voor de controle van de management- en control systemen, met de volgende aandachtsgebieden:
o De aanpak van fraude
o De verbetering van de IT-omgeving
o De effectiviteit en efficiëntie van de subsidieprocessen
• Motiveer je je controleteam middels een goede samenwerking en begeleid je hen inhoudelijk op:
o De analyses w.o. het uitvoeren van data-analyses, beoordelen van gedeclareerde kosten, subsidieaanvragen
o Het constateren en formuleren van bevindingen
o Het opbouwen van het feitencomplex
• Blijf je op de hoogte van nieuwe wet- en regelgeving vanuit de Europese Commissie die impact heeft op de normenkaders en jurisprudentie die van invloed is op de werkzaamheden.
• Draag je bij aan de verdere ontwikkeling van de Sector EU door controleaanpakken te vernieuwen, in-house trainingen te verzorgen en kennisdeling binnen de Sector EU te faciliteren.
• Ben je het aanspreekpunt voor zowel subsidieverstrekkers en uitvoeringsorganisaties, waarbij je hen op de hoogte houdt van de ontwikkelingen bij de onderzoeken/controles. Hierbij zorg je dat de verschillende belangen helder zijn en je jouw rug recht houdt bij conflicterende belangen. Daarnaast ben je het aanspreekpunt voor contacten vanuit Brussel en neem je deel aan vakinhoudelijke vergaderingen die de Europese Commissie verzorgt.
• Review je de uitgevoerde werkzaamheden als projectleider. Over lastige bevindingen spar je met de auditmanager, collega’s of bureau vaktechniek.

Dit bieden we nog meer

Naast het salaris ontvang je een individueel keuzebudget (IKB). Het IKB bestaat uit geld (16,5% van je brutojaarsalaris) en tijd. Met het IKB maak jij de keuzes die bij jou passen en kun je een deel van je arbeidsvoorwaarden zelf samenstellen. Je kunt er bijvoorbeeld voor kiezen om een deel van je maandinkomen te laten uitbetalen wanneer jij dat wenst. Ook kun je dit budget omzetten in verlof en andersom of besteden aan fiscaalvriendelijke doelen. De Rijksoverheid hecht sterk aan persoonlijke groei en loopbaanontwikkeling en biedt daarvoor tal van mogelijkheden. Tot de secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden behoren onder meer verschillende studiefaciliteiten, bedrijfsfitness, volledige vergoeding van je ov-reiskosten woon-werkverkeer en gedeeltelijk betaald ouderschapsverlof.

Dit vragen wij

  • Je hebt minimaal je postmaster accountancy behaald en hebt de praktijkopleiding tot RA (bijna) afgerond.
  • Je hebt minimaal vijf jaar actuele werkervaring binnen de externe audit of financiële auditpraktijk, bijvoorbeeld bij een accountantskantoor of interne auditdienst.
  • Ervaring met het aansturen en/of begeleiden van (kleine) auditteams.
  • Een kritische en analytische instelling, gecombineerd met organisatiesensitiviteit.
  • Het vermogen om collega's te motiveren en te stimuleren in hun professionele ontwikkeling.
  • Sterke samenwerkingsvaardigheden en het vermogen om teamleden te verbinden en gezamenlijk resultaten te behalen.

Kortom: Een dynamische rol waarbij je samen met jouw team toewerkt naar een kwalitatief uitgevoerde controle opdracht, waarvan de resultaten door de Auditdienst Rijk aan de Europese Commissie worden gerapporteerd. Voor een overzicht van de fondsen zie Fondsen Europa om de Hoek | Europa om de hoek.
Word jij de nieuwe collega van Ousama? Of wil je liever eerst eens praten over jouw misschien wel toekomstige werkzaamheden? Neem dan contact op met Suzanne Brom via 06 – 21 94 23 89.

Hier kom je te werken

Meer over jouw toekomstige plek in de organisatie

De Auditdienst Rijk (ADR) is de onafhankelijke interne auditdienst van de Rijksoverheid. In opdracht van alle ministeries onderzoeken wij of beleid, processen, systemen en geldstromen betrouwbaar, doelmatig en goed beheerst zijn. Daarmee helpen we de overheid om beter te functioneren en publiek geld zorgvuldig te besteden.

De ADR telt ruim zeshonderd medewerkers met verschillende achtergronden, zoals accountancy, bestuurskunde, IT, data-analyse, psychologie en kunstmatige intelligentie. Een groot deel werkt in de financial audit. Daarnaast werken collega’s als IT-auditor, operational auditor of auditor EU-fondsen.

De sector EU bestaat uit ruim 40 collega’s met verschillende expertises, ervaringen en achtergronden. Als auditor EU-fondsen werk je in één van de multidisciplinaire projectteams bestaande uit auditors met een diverse achtergrond, juristen, IT’ers en collega’s met projectmanagement vaardigheden. Natuurlijk is er ook ruimte om voor verschillende EU-fondsen werkzaamheden te verrichten. Kortom, je werkt in een divers en dynamisch team, waarbij persoonlijke en professionele groei centraal staan.

Er heerst een prettige, open en informele werksfeer, waarbij onderlinge samenwerking centraal staat. Jouw ontwikkeling is essentieel. Zo is er ook de mogelijkheid om naast je werk door te studeren, bijvoorbeeld door een post-masteropleiding tot registeraccountant te volgen of te continueren. Hierin neem je de verantwoordelijkheid voor je eigen kansen en ontwikkeling.

Audit EU-fondsen | Onze vakgebieden | Auditdienst Rijk

Over Ministerie van Financiën

Samen werken aan een financieel gezond Nederland

Het werk van het ministerie van Financiën gaat over meer dan cijfers en geld alleen. Het gaat over mensen zoals jij en ik. Mensen met verwachtingen, zorgen, vragen, dromen en plannen. We rekenen bijvoorbeeld allemaal op financiering voor goede zorg en goed onderwijs. Op duidelijkheid over belastingtarieven en op betrouwbare banken en verzekeraars, in Nederland en daarbuiten. En we rekenen allemaal op duidelijkheid over exportregels en wat we wel en niet mee mogen nemen vanuit de vakantiebestemming.

Het ministerie van Financiën luistert naar wat er speelt in de samenleving van vandaag en heeft aandacht voor hoe Nederlanders hun toekomst zien. Met die kennis en inzichten leggen we samen met andere ministeries en binnen ons internationale netwerk de juiste verbindingen en brengen we Nederland verder. We zorgen ervoor dat Nederland en onze economie klaar zijn voor de steeds sneller veranderende wereld van morgen. Op alle fronten. Dat gaat niet vanzelf. En natuurlijk is daar ook geld voor nodig. Dat geld brengen burgers en bedrijven via belastingen bijeen, en verdeelt de overheid over zaken die we als samenleving belangrijk vinden. Daarvoor moeten er keuzes worden gemaakt en worden ingegrepen als dat nodig is. Om ons land financieel gezond te houden, moet onze economie namelijk in balans blijven en tegelijk ook ruimte krijgen om te groeien.

Samen zorgen we ervoor dat er in Nederland kansen zijn voor welvaart en groei voor iedereen, vandaag, morgen en daarna. Samen werken we aan een financieel gezond Nederland.

Onze kernwaarden: integer, deskundig, duidelijk, durf en samenwerken zijn leidend voor ons gedrag en geven ons een gezamenlijke taal, waarmee we onderling bespreekbaar maken wat we doen en hoe we dat doen.

Lees meer over het ministerie van Financiën:

Bijzonderheden

We willen dat iedereen zich thuis voelt bij het ministerie van Financiën en zichzelf volledig kan ontwikkelen. Want samen werken aan een financieel gezond Nederland is waar we voor staan. Dit doen we vanuit verschillende perspectieven, achtergronden en inzichten, omdat we geloven dat dit onze denkkracht vergroot. Iedereen is welkom ongeacht culturele achtergrond, leeftijd, arbeidsvermogen, gender of seksuele geaardheid. Met jouw unieke bijdrage spelen we beter in op de behoeften uit onze samenleving.

  • Draag jij graag bij aan een financieel gezond Nederland? Je bent van harte welkom. Solliciteren kan door je cv en motivatie in te sturen. Maar we staan ook open voor andere vormen, zoals een video- (met bijgevoegd je cv) of presentatie-sollicitatie (in PowerPoint). In het laatste geval plak je de link van je sollicitatie in een pdf- of word-bestand. Zo kunnen we je sollicitatie goed verwerken.
  • De selectieprocedure bestaat uit twee gesprekken en een arbeidsvoorwaardengesprek. De eerste ronde sollicitatiegesprekken staat gepland op woensdag 2 december. De tweede ronde vindt plaats op dinsdag 8 december.
  • De inschaling voor deze functie vindt plaats op basis van kennis en ervaring.
  • De keuze voor een nieuwe baan kan best spannend zijn. We richten jouw overstap daarom zo persoonlijk mogelijk in. Via een introductiebijeenkomst en een onboarding app helpen we je om je weg te vinden en leer je hoe alles werkt binnen Financiën. Heb je nog vragen over de vacature of het selectieproces? Neem dan vooral contact met ons op. We helpen je graag in je overweging.
  • Wanneer je solliciteert op een functie maak je eenmalig een account aan. Met je account kan je de status van je sollicitatie inzien.
  • Wanneer de inschrijving van de vacature is gesloten zal de vacaturetekst online niet meer zichtbaar zijn. Mocht je deze op een later moment terug willen lezen dan adviseren wij je een kopie van de vacaturetekst op te slaan.
  • Heb je een studieschuld? Dan kun je vanaf 2025 maximaal € 2.000 per jaar aflossen met je Individueel Keuze Budget (IKB‐budget). Het aflossen van je studieschuld is een fiscaalvriendelijk doel. Dit betekent dat je over het bedrag wat je aan dit doel besteedt, geen belasting hoeft te betalen.

Waar jij aan werkt

Je beweegt je in het brede innovatie-ecosysteem en verbindt ondernemers, startups en scale-ups, kennisinstellingen, KTO’s, investeerders en andere partners. Je begrijpt wat nodig is om kennis en technologie verder te ontwikkelen, naar de markt te brengen en uit te bouwen tot succesvolle bedrijvigheid. Daarbij kijk je niet alleen naar de regeling zelf, maar ook naar de samenhang met andere vormen van ondersteuning, samenwerking en financiering.

Verder houd jij je bezig met het:

  • Zelfstandig uitvoeren van complexe opdrachten en projecten en regie voeren op de uitvoering van regelingen, zoals MIT R&D-samenwerkingsprojecten, PPS, TTT en VFF. Je bewaakt de voortgang en resultaten en stuurt waar nodig bij.
  • Adviseren van opdrachtgevers over de inrichting, uitvoering en doorontwikkeling van regelingen. Je vertaalt beleidsdoelen naar een effectieve en uitvoerbare aanpak die aansluit bij de behoeften van ondernemers, kennisinstellingen en andere partners.
  • Kennen van innovatie- en financieringsecosysteem en begrijpen wat startups, scale-ups en KTO’s nodig hebben om innovaties verder te ontwikkelen en naar de markt te brengen. Je hebt oog voor vraagstukken rond kennisvalorisatie, ondernemerschap, toegang tot kapitaal en de verschillende ontwikkelfasen van innovatieve bedrijven.
  • Bouwen en onderhouden van relaties binnen het ecosysteem en je verbindt kennisinstellingen, TKI’s, ondernemers, investeerders, financiers en andere partners. Je signaleert waar samenwerking of ondersteuning ontbreekt en benut kansen om partijen bij elkaar te brengen.
  • Analyseren van complexe vraagstukken, weegt belangen en risico’s af en adviseert over verbeteringen in regelingen, processen en samenwerking. Je kijkt daarbij ook naar de samenhang tussen instrumenten en financieringsmogelijkheden en naar de bijdrage die deze leveren aan innovatie en ondernemerschap.
  • Delen van kennis en ervaring met collega’s, werkt samen aan gezamenlijke resultaten en draagt bij aan de verdere professionalisering van het team en de kwaliteit en impact van onze dienstverlening.

Dit bieden we nog meer

Naast het salaris ontvang je een individueel keuzebudget (IKB). Het IKB bestaat uit geld (16,5% van je brutojaarsalaris) en tijd. Met het IKB maak jij de keuzes die bij jou passen en kun je een deel van je arbeidsvoorwaarden zelf samenstellen. Je kunt er bijvoorbeeld voor kiezen om een deel van je maandinkomen te laten uitbetalen wanneer jij dat wenst. Ook kun je dit budget omzetten in verlof en andersom of besteden aan fiscaalvriendelijke doelen. De Rijksoverheid hecht sterk aan persoonlijke groei en loopbaanontwikkeling en biedt daarvoor tal van mogelijkheden. Tot de secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden behoren onder meer verschillende studiefaciliteiten, bedrijfsfitness, volledige vergoeding van je ov-reiskosten woon-werkverkeer en gedeeltelijk betaald ouderschapsverlof.

Dit vragen wij

Je kunt zelfstandig werken en beslissingen nemen. Je toont initiatief en verantwoordelijkheid voor je eigen taken. Daarnaast, beschik je over sterke communicatieve vaardigheden, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. Je bent een stevige gesprekspartner voor opdrachtgevers en uitvoeringspartners. Je overziet complexe vraagstukken, voert zelfstandig regie op opdrachten en projecten en draagt bij aan de verdere ontwikkeling en effectiviteit van onze dienstverlening.

Verder heb je:

  • Wo-werk-en-denkniveau in een technische en/of innovatie gerelateerde richting.
  • Minimaal 2 jaar werkervaring met project- en programmamanagement.
  • Aantoonbare affiniteit met kennis, innovatie en ondernemerschap.
  • Aantoonbare kennis van het ecosysteem (KTO’s, TKI’s, startups, scale-ups en investeerders).
  • Ervaring met het MKB/ondernemers.

Hier kom je te werken

Meer over jouw toekomstige plek in de organisatie

Binnen Kennis, Innovatie & Ondernemerschap (KIO) werken we aan het versterken van innovatie en ondernemerschap in Nederland. We verbinden beleid, kennis en praktijk en ondersteunen ondernemers en andere partijen bij het ontwikkelen en toepassen van vernieuwende oplossingen voor maatschappelijke vraagstukken. Dat doen we met uiteenlopende regelingen en opdrachten, in samenwerking met opdrachtgevers, bedrijven, kennisinstellingen en andere partners.

Onze opdrachten zijn divers en vaak complex. Dat vraagt om inhoudelijke expertise, een ondernemende houding en het vermogen om samen tot resultaat te komen. Binnen ons team krijg je de ruimte om zelfstandig verantwoordelijkheid te nemen, mee te denken over verbeteringen en bij te dragen aan de verdere ontwikkeling van onze dienstverlening.

Je komt terecht in een divers en collegiaal team binnen een open werksfeer waar kennisdeling centraal staat. Je werkt samen met collega’s uit verschillende disciplines aan actuele maatschappelijke opgaven. Geen dag is hetzelfde – maar elke dag draagt bij aan een sterker, innovatiever MKB.

We werken hybride. Als team komen we op de maandag, dinsdag en donderdagen samen op ons kantoor in Den Haag. Voor de overige dagen kan je vanaf elke locatie jouw werk doen (vanuit huis, kantoor of elders).

Over Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland (RVO)

Vandaag werken aan de wereld van morgen

De wereld verandert elke dag en wij veranderen mee. Met ruim 6500 RVO’ers werken we iedere dag aan morgen. We ondersteunen, adviseren en stimuleren ondernemend Nederland. We helpen met innoveren en verduurzamen. Nationaal en internationaal, want ons werk stopt niet bij de grens. Samen werken we aan:

  • De verduurzaming van onze energievoorzieningen.
  • Het tegengaan van klimaatverandering.
  • Een omslag naar een duurzaam landbouw- en voedselsysteem.
  • Een sterke digitale economie.

Het zijn grote uitdagingen, maar wij geloven dat het mogelijk is, en durven de uitdaging aan te gaan. Om te bouwen aan het Nederland van morgen verbinden we ondernemers, overheden en organisaties.

We doen het samen.

Wat doen we?

Wij maken overheidsbeleid bereikbaar en uitvoerbaar. Van voorlichting, advies en financiering tot het bieden van een luisterend oor voor ondernemers en organisaties. En dat is nog maar een klein onderdeel van wat we doen. Ondernemend Nederland is ontzettend veelzijdig en daarom zijn wij dat ook.

Divers maakt beter

Met enorme uitdagingen op komst, is de juiste mensen aan boord hebben belangrijk. Het maakt bij ons niet uit wie je bent. Wij kijken naar wat je kunt en waar jouw ambities liggen. Om de wereld duurzamer te maken hebben we ideeën nodig uit alle hoeken van de samenleving. We geven je vertrouwen, autonomie en verantwoordelijkheid. Want zo boek jij samen met collega’s de mooiste resultaten. Voor jezelf, voor ondernemers en voor morgen.

Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland (RVO)

  • Bij RVO werken we hybride. Voor deze functie wordt van je verwacht dat je 2 keer per week op de RVO-vestiging in Den Haag. aanwezig bent. Voor de overige dagen kun je je werk vanaf elke locatie doen (vanuit huis, op één van de RVO-kantoren of elders).

Sollicitatieproces

Selectieproces

  • Alle binnengekomen cv’s worden beoordeeld aan de hand van de eisen uit de vacature. Zorg dus dat uit jouw cv duidelijk wordt of je over de benodigde eisen beschikt.
  • Binnen 5 werkdagen na sluiting van de vacature ontvang je een reactie.
  • De gesprekken zijn gepland in Den Haag.
  • De sollicitatiegesprekken staan in het teken van, de in de vacature genoemde, competenties. Dit doen we a.d.h.v. competentiegerichte vragen.

Dienstverband

  • In eerste instantie krijg je een contract voor bepaalde tijd, afhankelijk van functioneren én ontwikkelingen in opdrachten kan het zijn dat je een vast contract krijgt.

Rijkskandidaten

  • Ben je Van-Werk-Naar-Werk- of (medisch) herplaatsingskandidaat binnen de Rijksoverheid? Voeg dan na het ontvangen van de bevestigingsmail van je sollicitatie de aanwijzingsbrief toe bij ‘Extra documenten’.
  • Heb je een contract voor onbepaalde tijd, dan behoud je deze. Bij een tijdelijke vacature bieden wij jou dan de mogelijkheid voor een detachering.

title: Guest Relation Supervisor
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Process all guest check-ins, verifying guest identity, form of payment, assigning room, and activating/issuing room key. Set up accurate accounts for each guest according to their requirements. Enter Marriott Rewards information. Ensure rates match market codes, document exceptions. Secure payment prior to issuing room key, verify/adjust billing. Compile and review daily reports/logs/contingency lists. Complete cashier and closing reports. Supply guests with directions and property information. Accommodate guest requests, contacting appropriate staff if necessary. Follow up to ensure requests have been met. Process all payment types, vouchers, paid-outs, and charges. Balance and drop receipts. Count and secure bank at beginning and end of shift. Obtain manual authorizations and follow all Accounting procedures. Notify Loss Prevention/Security of any guest reports of theft.

Assist management in training, evaluating, counseling, motivating and coaching employees; serve as a role model and first point of contact of the Guarantee of Fair Treatment/Open Door Policy process. Develop/maintain positive working relationships; support team to reach common goals; listen and respond appropriately to employee concerns. Follow company policies and procedures; report accidents, injuries, and unsafe work conditions to manager; complete safety training and certifications; ensure personal appearance is clean and professional; maintain confidentiality of proprietary information; protect company assets. Welcome and acknowledge guests; anticipate and address guests’ service needs; assist individuals with disabilities; thank guests with genuine appreciation. Speak using clear and professional language; prepare and review written documents accurately and completely; answer telephones using appropriate etiquette. Ensure adherence to quality standards. Enter and locate information using computers/POS systems. Stand, sit, or walk for an extended period of time. Move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 10 pounds without assistance. Perform other reasonable job duties as requested by Supervisors.

Education: High school diploma or G.E.D. equivalent.

Related Work Experience: At least 1 year of related work experience.

Supervisory Experience: At least 1 year of supervisory experience.

License or Certification: None

title: Editorial Content Specialist
description:
Turing is looking for candidates who have solid experience in editing, content curation, or publishing, particularly at the level expected for experienced editors or media professionals responsible for maintaining editorial quality and publication standards.

Role Overview:
  • In this role, you will be working on projects to help evaluate and improve AI using your editorial expertise and communication skills.
  • No prior AI experience is required.
  • These projects will help you learn how to leverage AI to enhance editing workflows, improve content quality, and optimize publishing operations.

What Does Day-to-Day Look Like:
  • Design and solve real-world editorial and publishing scenarios to test AI reasoning.
  • Write clear, structured examples covering grammar correction, tone alignment, structural editing, and content refinement.
  • Evaluate AI responses for accuracy, editorial quality, and adherence to professional standards.
  • Collaborate with AI researchers to strengthen model understanding of editing, writing tone, and publishing conventions.

Requirements:
  • 4+ years of experience as an Editor, Copy Editor, or Content Specialist in publishing, media, or communications.
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in English, Journalism, Communications, Media Studies, or a related field.
  • Strong English writing, grammar, and editorial judgment skills.
  • Ability to explain editing choices and language nuances clearly and effectively.

Perks of freelancing with Turing & offer details:
  • Strong compensation (exact amount varies by project).
  • Work in a fully remote environment.
  • Engagement type: Contractor assignment/freelancer, potentially full-time.
  • Duration of projects: approximately 1 month (with possibility for extension).

What Turing is NOT seeking from your expertise:
  • Confidential or proprietary information from any employer, university, etc.
  • Trade secrets or internal company or university data.
  • Specific client information or case details.
  • Any information that would violate NDAs, employment agreements or other confidentiality obligations.

About Turing:
Based in San Francisco, California, Turing is the world’s leading research accelerator for frontier AI labs and a trusted partner for global enterprises deploying advanced AI systems. Turing supports customers in two ways: first, by accelerating frontier research with high-quality data, advanced training pipelines, plus top AI researchers who specialize in coding, reasoning, STEM, multilinguality, multimodality, and agents; and second, by applying that expertise to help enterprises transform AI from proof of concept into proprietary intelligence with systems that perform reliably, deliver measurable impact, and drive lasting results on the P&L.

title: Professional Teaching Fellow - Medical Imaging
description:
Te Whiwhinga mahi | The opportunity

We are seeking a qualified Medical Imaging Technologist (MIT) to join the Department of Anatomy and Medical Imaging as a Professional Teaching Fellow, contributing to the clinical coordination and programme delivery of Bachelor of Medical Imaging (Honours), starting in 2027.

The role aims to strengthen engagement with students and clinical partners, enhance pastoral and educational support during placements, and contribute to the effective administration and coordination of clinical learning activities across New Zealand.

Ngā kawenga matua | Key responsibilities

  • Support the delivery of academic and clinical teaching and learning within the Medical Imaging programme.
  • Coordinate and support student clinical placements across New Zealand.
  • Provide guidance and pastoral support to students during their clinical training.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clinical educators and placement providers.
  • Assist with clinical tutorials, simulation activities, and student assessment processes.
  • Contribute to programme development, quality improvement initiatives, and student success activities

This is a part time (20h per week), fixed term (3 years) opportunity.

The salary range for this role is $105,791 - $139,199 (pro-rated) based on skills and experience.

For more detailed information, please refer to the Position Description

He kōrero mōu | About you

You are a clinically credible Medical Imaging Technologist who is passionate about education and supporting adult learners in workplace‑based clinical environments. You enjoy working collaboratively with clinicians and academic colleagues and are motivated by the opportunity to help support the clinical training of student MIT’s.

You bring strong communication and organisational skills, a learner‑centred teaching approach, and a commitment to high‑quality, equitable and culturally responsive education

You will also bring:

  • Bachelor degree in Medical Imaging or equivalent recognised by the Medical Radiation Technologists Board (MRTB) of New Zealand.
  • A current New Zealand clinical annual practising certificate (APC) in Medical Imaging.
  • Recent clinical experience in Medical Imaging clinical environment.
  • Understand the significance of the Treaty of Waitangi, with a commitment to culturalism.
  • Strong organisational and administrative abilities.

The University of Auckland is New Zealand’s leading university and maintains significant computational, laboratory and analytic facilities. Auckland itself is frequently rated as one of the world’s most liveable cities.

title: Stretch Practitioner
description:
At Stretch Zone, we’re redefining what it means to work in bodywork and recovery. If you love the hands-on impact of assisted stretching and helping people move and feel better in their bodies—this is your opportunity to turn that passion into a long-term, growth-focused career. We’re not just another wellness studio. Stretch Zone is a rapidly growing national brand built around practitioner-assisted stretching—a proven, science-backed approach that improves mobility, reduces pain, and helps people live better every day. Our proprietary method and patented strapping equipment allow you to deliver results members can feel immediately, all while working in a supportive, high-energy environment focused on personal and professional growth.

What makes this role especially exciting? We provide paid, in-house certification and training, so you can expand your skillset, deepen your understanding of the body, and build a sustainable career in wellness.

From day one, you’ll be part of a team that’s passionate about helping people feel their best—while giving you the tools, education, and career path to grow right alongside us. If you’re ready to do meaningful work, stay hands-on, and be part of a movement that’s changing lives—welcome to Stretch Zone.

What You Have:

  • Background or experience in exercise science or bodywork (preferred)
  • Able to complete hands-on and virtual training
  • Desire to help others achieve their lifestyle goals
  • Reliable transportation
What You'll Do:
  • Deliver individualized stretching sessions to members in alignment with your Stretch Zone Certification
  • Accurately assess members' needs to determine correct protocols
  • Provide exceptional hospitality and customer service daily

About Stretch Zone
  • Using our patented equipment, Stretch Zone practitioners follow specific protocols to help our members enjoy an increase in athletic performance, range of motion, reduced stiffness, and improved reaction time.

title: Solutions Architect (Japan)
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Solutions Architecture Team partners with our users to realize their full potential through the adoption of prescriptive solutions that drive their growth and success. We influence revenue growth across Stripe’s product portfolio, and collaborate with sales, support, product management, and Stripe’s executive team to provide the best experience to our most valued customers.

What you’ll do

As a member of the team, the Solutions Architect will build highly consultative trusted relationships with c-level executives and technical decision makers in the customer’s organization to provide business and technical thought leadership, and become a trusted advisor in solving mission-critical business challenges. She/he will architect business models with them so they can drive new monetization opportunities and growth for both the user and Stripe.

Responsibilities

  • Drive Account Growth & Expansion:
    • Find and articulate opportunities to grow the product's use within existing accounts, extending its footprint into new global markets or business units.
    • Close complex deals and accelerate the adoption of new features and products.
  • Serve as a Trusted Advisor:
