    • Be a thought leader and trusted advisor to senior executives (like the CIO, CTO, and Head of Product/Payments).
  • Team Collaboration:
    • Be an integral member of the account team, deeply involved in defining the strategy for key customers.
    • Collaborate closely with Account Executives, Professional Services, Customer Success Managers, Partners, Technical Account Managers and Product Teams to develop and execute on the account strategy for Stripe’s platform prospects.

Who you are

You have achieved an experienced position as an enterprise architect, senior solution architect or solution engineer and have a successful track record advising enterprise-grade digital native / SAAS / Platform / Marketplace companies, focused on identifying business priorities, formulating technology strategies and designing an end-to-end business solution. You possess deep technical acumen, high interpersonal and leadership skills, and have demonstrated the ability to become a trusted advisor to senior executives and facilitate customer success along the entire customer journey. Strategic and creative thinker who can proactively identify challenges, take ownership, and maintain a positive approach when facing difficult obstacles.

Minimum requirements

  • 7+ years of experience in a similar customer-facing engineering role such as sales engineer, pre-sale solution consultant or solutions architect for a global software enterprise.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills in English and Japanese to work with Japanese merchants
  • Executive engagement skills and presence, with an ability to establish strong relationships with key decision makers and build credibility at all levels.
  • Effective group-facilitation skills and confidence in proposing and leading customer meetings to gain strategic footing and pursue opportunities.
  • Thorough understanding of the software development lifecycle and API architectures. A background in writing code in any of Stripe’s primary deployment languages (Ruby, Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, etc.) is a plus.
  • Outstanding spoken and written communication skills, presentation skills, and confident in explaining complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to operate independently in a highly ambiguous and fast-paced environment
  • Passion to take on ownership and drive change in a constantly evolving environment.
  • Ability to travel per business needs

Preferred qualifications

title: Senior Control Systems Engineer
description:
What if you could do the kind of work the world needs?

At WSP, you can access our global scale, contribute to landmark projects and connect with the brightest minds in your field to do the best work of your life. You can embrace your curiosity in a culture that celebrates new ideas and diverse perspectives. You can experience a world of opportunity and the chance to shape a career as unique as you.

At WSP you’ll find the scale and reach you need to do the kind of work the world needs – and the culture and people that make it the best work of your life.

Our Mining & Metals group is a leader in future-led end to end mining solutions and delivery of services to our clients. We specialise in delivering comprehensive and tailored solutions for the mining industry. Our team manages and executes large-scale capital projects, ensuring they are completed on time, within budget, and to the highest standards of quality and safety and leave a lasting positive legacy in the communities we engage with.

What you’ll do:

We are seeking an experienced Senior Control Systems Engineer to join our Brisbane Mining team on an initial 12 month contract, to play a key role in the design, development, commissioning and support of industrial control systems across a diverse portfolio of mining and resources projects.

This is a senior, hands-on engineering position suited to someone who enjoys taking ownership of control system solutions from concept and detailed design through to implementation and commissioning.

You’ll work as part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary engineering team supporting projects across the mining lifecycle, with exposure to brownfield upgrades, sustaining capital and project delivery environments across a range of commodities.

  • Design, develop and implement PLC, SCADA and HMI control systems.

  • Develop control philosophies, functional descriptions, I/O lists, network architectures and technical documentation.

  • PLC and HMI/SCADA programming, configuration and testing.

  • Lead or support FAT, SAT and site commissioning activities.

  • Troubleshoot complex control, instrumentation, communications and automation issues.

  • Review engineering designs and provide technical guidance to project teams and junior engineers.

  • Coordinate with electrical, instrumentation, process, mechanical and project engineering disciplines.

  • Engage with clients, suppliers and contractors to deliver practical and reliable engineering solutions.

  • Ensure designs comply with relevant engineering standards, project specifications and safety requirements.

  • Support estimation, planning and delivery of control system work packages.

About you:

  • Degree in Electrical, Electronic, Mechatronic, Control Systems Engineering or a related discipline.

  • Strong professional experience in industrial automation and control systems.

  • Demonstrated PLC and SCADA/HMI engineering capability.

  • Experience with industrial communications and networked control systems.

  • Strong troubleshooting and commissioning skills.

  • Ability to interpret electrical drawings, P&IDs, control philosophies and functional specifications.

  • Strong documentation and technical communication skills.

  • Experience with platforms such as Rockwell Automation / Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Schneider Electric, Honeywell, Emerson or ABB would be advantageous.

Why WSP?

  • Variety of work across mining and resources projects, clients and commodities.

  • End-to-end project exposure, from studies and detailed design through to commissioning and operational support.

  • The opportunity to own control system solutions and influence key technical decisions.

  • Close collaboration with electrical, instrumentation, process, mechanical and project engineering specialists.

  • Exposure to complex brownfield and operational environments, where practical and reliable engineering solutions make a real difference.

  • The opportunity to mentor and provide technical guidance to developing engineers while remaining hands-on technically.

  • Be part of a well-established and supportive local team, with flexible working arrangements and strong focus on wellbeing

If you’re looking for a role that combines hands-on control systems engineering with technical leadership and project variety, this is an opportunity to take on a senior position where you can genuinely influence how solutions are developed and delivered.

You’ll have the opportunity to work with experienced engineers across multiple disciplines while building your profile as a senior technical specialist within our Mining business.

title: Senior Technical Officer - Magnetic Resonance
description:
• Part time (0.6 FTE), fixed term until 27th December 2027
  • Exciting opportunity to support world-class research infrastructure and advanced magnetic resonance technologies
  • Base Salary $117,133 + 17% superannuation – Pro-Rata to 0.6FTE

About the opportunity

Sydney Analytical is the largest facility of its kind in Australia, with new leading-edge equipment for vibrational and X-ray spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, X-ray and light scattering, drug discovery and magnetic resonance. We provide equipment access and expert technical guidance to support researchers’ most challenging problems. In addition to our main characterisation methods, we offer precision cutting and polishing, high-temperature thermal analysis and customised controlled environment options.

As the Senior Technical Officer - Magnetic Resonance, you will play a critical role in supporting the operation, development and optimisation of advanced magnetic resonance facilities that underpin cutting-edge research and teaching activities. Working within Sydney Analytical, you will provide expert technical support, training and advice to researchers, students and academic staff, ensuring the successful delivery of research projects and laboratory-based learning.

You will oversee the day-to-day management of specialised magnetic resonance instrumentation and laboratory facilities, contribute to the design and implementation of experimental protocols, and drive best-practice laboratory operations. You will also play an important role in maintaining safe, compliant and efficient research environments while fostering collaborative relationships across a diverse research community

Your key responsibilities will be to:

  • collaborate with other professional and academic staff to provide user support and advice across a range of specialist equipment focussed on small molecule and chemical applications of solution-state NMR spectroscopy.
  • support the day-to-day operational aspects of Sydney Analytical laboratory equipment
  • provide sound, expert technical support and advice to researchers and students using the research facilities, aiding the research and teaching work and providing collaborative research input for projects being undertaken by the work area
  • ensure the laboratory is properly maintained and compliant with Workplace Health and Safety requirements

About you

  • a keen interest and experience in the support of a vast range of NMR equipment
  • excellent communication skills and a passion for training new users in specialised equipment
  • tertiary qualifications in Chemistry, Engineering or Physics
  • postgraduate qualifications utilising NMR applications preferred
  • working knowledge of safety regulations and experience in implementing safety procedures in a multiuser environment
  • advanced computer skills, including high level knowledge of commercial NMR software, data analytics and workflow technologies.

title: Director of Engineering
description:
JOB SUMMARY

Provides a high level of property maintenance knowledge. Position has overall responsibility for maintaining the building, grounds and physical plant with particular attention towards safety, security and asset protection. Accountable for managing the budget, capital expenditure projects, preventative maintenance and energy conservation. Develops and implements strategies that will deliver products and services, which meet or exceed the needs and expectations of guests and employees while maximizing the financial performance. Responsible for maintaining standards and regulatory requirements. Leads the emergency response team for all facility issues.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or GED; 6 years experience in the engineering and maintenance or related professional area; technical training in HVAC-R/Electrical/Plumbing.

OR

• 2-year degree from an accredited university in Building and Construction, Engineering, Mechanics, or related major; 4 years experience in the engineering and maintenance or related professional area; technical training in HVAC-R/Electrical/Plumbing.

CORE WORK ACTIVITIES

Managing Engineering Operations and Budgets

• Works with property and regional engineering leadership team to determine how Engineering is performing against budget and highlights areas of concern to leadership.

• Manages the physical plant including equipment, refrigeration, HVAC, plumbing, water treatment and electrical systems in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures.

• Administers service contracts to support property needs.

• Ensures fire crew has complete understanding of all procedures, equipment and alarms.

• Coaches and supports engineering leadership team to effectively manage controllable expenses (e.g., wages, heat, light and power, water consumption, tools and equipment, grounds keeping supplies, uniforms, vendors, service agreements, inventory, etc.).

• Manages and controls heat, light and power.

• Develops an engineering operating strategy that is aligned with the property/brand’s business strategy.

• Develops and manages Engineering budget.

• Ensures integration of departmental goals in game plans.

• Oversees execution of long term preventative maintenance and 10 year asset protection plans.

• Reviews financial reports and statements to determine how Engineering is performing against budget.

• Addresses potential areas of concern and proposing solutions to owners in a proactive manner.

• Communicates a clear and consistent message regarding departmental goals to produce desired results.

• Supervises construction to ensure timely completion of projects within budgetary guidelines.

Maintaining Engineering Standards

• Ensures compliance with state, local and federal regulations.

• Maintains property life safety systems (e.g., fire fighting equipment, sprinkler systems, and alarm systems).

• Ensures building and equipment licenses, permits and certifications are current.

• Ensures property policies are administered fairly and consistently.

Managing Profitability

• Manages areas of operation to budget by reviewing operating statements, budget worksheets and payroll progress reports.

• Monitors and manages the payroll function.

• Manages department's controllable expenses to achieve or exceed budgeted goals.

• Participates in the development of department's capital expenditure goals; manages projects as needed.

• Participates in the budgeting process for areas of responsibility.

• Prepares weekly and period end P&L critiques.

• Understands the impact of department's operation on the overall property financial goals; educates staff on details as appropriate.

• Reviews and manages controllable expenses such as, heat, light, power, water consumption, tools and equipment, grounds keeping supplies, uniforms, vendors, service agreements, etc.

Conducting Human Resources Activities

• Ensures employees are treated fairly and equitably.

• Ensures disciplinary procedures and documentation are completed according to Standard and Local Operating Procedures (SOPs and LSOPs) and support the Peer Review Process.

• Utilizes employee feedback and an “open door” policy to identify and address employee problems or concerns in a timely manner.

• Celebrates successes by publicly recognizing the contributions of team members.

• Resolves guest problems and complaints.

• Brings issues to the attention of Human Resources as necessary.

• Ensures that regular on-going communication takes place throughout the engineering operation to communicate daily operations activities, set expectations and create awareness of business objectives.

title: Injury and Claims Manager
description:
About the team

You’ll lead the WorkCover team, comprising Senior Injury and Claims Advisors, Injury and Claims Advisors and WorkCover administration support. Working closely with People & Culture, managers, stores, distribution centres, insurers, legal representatives and rehabilitation providers, the team manages workers' compensation claims and supports effective return-to-work outcomes across the business.

About the department

The WHS and WorkCover department plays an important role in supporting workplace safety, injury management and compliance across the business. The department provides guidance and oversight to ensure our people are supported following workplace injuries, while helping the organisation meet its legislative obligations and maintain safe working environments.

Key responsibilities

  • Oversee the end-to-end management of complex workers' compensation and personal injury claims, including claim notifications, investigations, liability decisions, treatment plans, injured worker payments and lump-sum settlements.

  • Develop and implement proactive return-to-work plans in partnership with injured team members, managers, medical practitioners and rehabilitation providers to achieve sustainable outcomes.

  • Provide strategic advice to senior management on claims trends, injury management, liability exposure, legislative requirements and opportunities to reduce workers' compensation premiums.

  • Manage insurance policies and premium requirements across the business and franchise network, ensuring policies remain accurate and current and premiums are paid within required timeframes.

  • Monitor claims performance, identify trends and prepare reporting and insights to support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.

  • Build and maintain effective relationships with insurers, legal representatives, rehabilitation providers and internal stakeholders to support positive claims outcomes.

  • Lead, coach and develop the WorkCover team, setting clear expectations, managing performance and supporting individual development and capability.

  • Drive improvements to claims management processes, governance and compliance, ensuring consistent application of workers' compensation legislation and internal policies.

  • Oversee the team's operational priorities, ensuring appropriate resources, workflows and support are in place to meet business requirements.

Who we are looking for

  • At least five years' experience in a senior WorkCover or workers' compensation role, with strong knowledge of claims management principles and relevant legislation.

  • Demonstrated experience managing complex claims, return-to-work strategies, insurance policies and premiums, with experience using the Solv Injury platform.

  • Strong leadership, strategic thinking and stakeholder management skills, with excellent communication, organisation and time management capabilities and the ability to manage competing priorities.

Why Join Us?

Grow your career with purpose – Access a wide range of learning and development programs, including our internally designed leadership pathway to support your long‑term growth. Be part of a purpose-driven organisation making a difference in healthcare, working with a collaborative and supportive team.

Be rewarded for your impact – Enjoy annual salary reviews linked to your performance, recognising the value you bring to the team.

Flexibility that works – Work from home one day per week, while staying connected with your team at our vibrant Preston Support Office four days a week. We’re committed to supporting our people through life’s important moments. Alongside our formal flexibility policies, we recognise that some circumstances, such as returning from parental leave or managing personal wellbeing may require additional consideration. In these situations, we work collaboratively on case‑by‑case arrangements to provide the support needed while balancing the requirements of the role and team.

Paid parental leave – We support growing families with six weeks of paid parental leave for primary carers and one week of paid parental leave for secondary carers.

Exclusive savings – Access generous employee discounts across a wide range of products with our partnership with Flare, including company-wide corporate offers on healthcare premiums with Bupa Healthcare, banking benefits with Comm Bank and novated leasing.

Support when you need it – Tap into confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) services for personal or professional support.

Take advantage of our subsidised and convenient onsite canteen for varied and affordable meals, coffee, confectionary and bakery items.

Easy commuting – Enjoy our complimentary shuttle bus connecting nearby train stations to the Preston Support Office, making public transport travel simple and stress‑free.

About Us

Sigma Healthcare is powering pharmacy! We have the largest pharmacy network in Australia with trusted brands including Chemist Warehouse, Amcal, Discount Drug Stores and Ultra Beauty! We are powered by our dedicated people and our leading Australian full line pharmacy wholesale and distribution business that delivers medicines to any pharmacy anywhere in Australia. With Chemist Warehouse now operating in four countries outside Australia, we continue to expand our reach.

How to Apply!

If you're ready to join a team that is shaping the future of healthcare and retail, click Apply Now to visit our Careers Page and submit your application.

Sigma Healthcare is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and respectful workplace where everyone can thrive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences and encourage you to apply, even if you don't meet every requirement listed.

title: Market Access-Head of SPC MA Strategy, China-Shanghai
description:
JOB PURPOSE:


The Head of SPC MA Strategy, China is responsible for the development and implementation of market access, pricing strategies, and health economics evidence generation specifically for Sanofi's Specialty portfolio in China. This role focuses on securing optimal access, pricing, and reimbursement conditions for SPC products from early phases to launch and throughout the lifecycle, while developing robust HEOR evidence to support these strategies. The role holder will work closely with local cross-functional teams, global Specialty Care teams, and HEOR teams to optimize patient access strategy and ensure business sustainability for the SPC portfolio.


KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:


1. Specialty Care Market Access Strategy


• Accountable for the definition of the Value & Access Strategy/Pricing strategy for SPC portfolio, aligned with local cross-functional teams and coordinates the implementation of the access strategy at a country level

• Ensures that local deliverables (Value Story/Price/reimbursement/HE dossier) and payer marketing actions/materials for SPC products are ready in a timely manner

• Work cross-functionally to deliver insights and anticipate market access evolution, developing market access strategies aligned with clinical evidence, patient needs, and commercial ambition for SPC portfolio

• Lead the development of payer value propositions for SPC products and perform gap analyses to direct the development of Value Pack and Market Access toolkits in co-creation with the SPC BU, Medical, PA and Policy teams

• Maintain strong partnership with GMAx to maximize value offering to payers for SPC products and share best practices

• Create long-range strategies and tactics specific to SPC therapeutic areas to understand the evolution of access evidence needs and identify appropriate capabilities and resources

• Perform gap assessments for local capacity and capabilities based on SPC business opportunities and engage with internal stakeholders for resource allocations

• Build capability to interact with external think tanks to shape P&R environment for Specialty Care products

• Lead HEOR strategy development for SPC portfolio aligned with business objectives and market access needs

• Identify HEOR evidence gaps and develop research plans to address unmet evidence needs for SPC access decision-making

• Provide HEOR inputs to the strategic and operational planning processes for SPC products


2. SPC Portfolio Pricing and Market Access Execution


• Develop price & reimbursement strategy with optimal conditions for SPC product launches and portfolio market maintenance

• Secure alignment on pricing strategy and decisions between SPC business units and GMAx

• Develop innovative solutions and dossiers to support reimbursement negotiation and other access practices specific to SPC therapeutic areas

• Provide strategic inputs to SPC business teams on national reimbursement, provincial reimbursement, and innovative access solutions

• Build strong engagement platforms and partnerships for access with KOLs in therapeutic areas relevant to SPC portfolio

• Help global SPC counterparts understand China's market, payment environment, and specific considerations for Specialty Care products

• Oversee the design, execution, and publication of health economic models, budget impact analyses, cost-effectiveness studies, and real-world evidence studies specific to SPC products

• Develop evidence-based arguments and recommendations for pricing and reimbursement strategies using HEOR methodologies

• Ensure HEOR deliverables (HE dossiers, economic models, evidence synthesis) are developed with high quality and in a timely manner to support SPC market access milestones


3. HEOR Evidence Generation & Stakeholder Engagement


• Lead the development and execution of HEOR evidence generation for SPC portfolio to support national reimbursement, provincial reimbursement, innovative solutions, and medical expense management

• Build strong engagement platforms and partnerships with key opinion leaders in health economics, HTA, and outcomes research areas relevant to SPC therapeutic areas

• Develop collaborative relationships with academic institutions, research organizations, and payer communities to advance HEOR science for Specialty Care

• Interact with external think tanks and policy makers to shape the HEOR and HTA environment for SPC products in China

• Represent Sanofi SPC at external HEOR conferences, advisory boards, and professional forums

• Help global counterparts understand China's health-economic and payment environment for Specialty Care based on economic studies and policy analysis


4. Team Leadership and Capability Building


• Manage high-performing SPC market access team members

• Support talent development and drive capability building in SPC market access areas

• Foster collaboration across SPC portfolio and with cross-functional teams

• Drive capability building in HEOR methodologies, tools, and best practices across the SPC organization

• Perform gap assessments for local HEOR capacity and capabilities based on SPC business opportunities

• Collaborate with central HEOR team, Medical Affairs, Commercial, and Public Affairs teams to ensure HEOR evidence is integrated into SPC value propositions


JOB-HOLDER REQUIREMENTS:


Education:

• Public health, medical, pharmacy, or health economics background

• Master's degree in medical, public health, health economics, or related field; PhD in such areas is preferred


Experience & knowledge & Competencies:

• At least 10+ years of working experience in pharmaceutical or healthcare industry

• 5+ years working experience in Market Access & pricing in multinational pharmaceutical companies, with experience in Specialty Care portfolio preferred

• 3+ years of people management experience

• Comprehensive understanding of China healthcare system and global Market Access trends, particularly for Specialty Care products

• Deep understanding of pharmaceutical pricing/access/funding, payer needs and stakeholder management in Specialty Care therapeutic areas

• Strategic thinking and project management skills

• Problem solving and conflict management skills

• Strong teamwork spirit & collaborative approach including ability to be successful in a matrix environment

• Excellent communication skills with the ability to communicate persuasively verbally and in writing with fluency in English and Mandarin

• Ability to master complexity and work under pressure

• Good command of both written and oral English

Pursue progress, discover extraordinary

Better is out there. Better medications, better outcomes, better science. But progress doesn’t happen without people – people from different backgrounds, in different locations, doing different roles, all united by one thing: a desire to make miracles happen. So, let’s be those people.

title: Counterintelligence Analyst - Active Clearance Required
description:
We're looking for a Counterintelligence (CI) Analyst within the Counterintelligence Program to conduct counterintelligence and counterterrorism research, analysis, reporting, collaboration, training, and information management to identify threats and support national security stakeholders. You will report to the Supervisory Analyst.

This position offers a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You will have the flexibility to work from home one day per week on non-Alternate Work Schedule work week.

This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level.

You will

  • Conduct research and analysis supporting diverse counterintelligence and counterterrorism investigations under direction of senior staff.
  • Collect, analyze, and fuse information from open and secure sources to identify threats and assess foreign capabilities.
  • Provide analytical support to threat assessments and tactical and strategic intelligence products for local and national stakeholders.
  • Support or prepare briefings, debriefings, and presentations concerning foreign nationals, foreign travel, and CI/CT risks.
  • Support DOE data calls, programmatic initiatives, plans, and proposed policy changes.
  • Contribute to collaborations with Laboratory organizations, DOE, national laboratories, the U.S. Intelligence Community (USIC), and law enforcement.
  • Contribute to and deliver counterintelligence awareness and training materials.
  • Enter, retrieve, and manage information in Laboratory and USIC analytical and investigative systems.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Additional job responsibilities, at the K02.2 level

  • Independently conduct comprehensive research and complex counterintelligence analysis with limited direction.
  • Produce complex threat assessments and intelligence products.
  • Participate in and, as appropriate, lead collaborative analytical projects.
  • Provide general direction to support staff and junior analysts.
  • Assist senior staff in developing recommendations on programmatic and policy matters.
  • This position requires an active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at the time of hire.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access. Please note that any current active Q or Top Secret clearance with DOE does not guarantee DOE SCI access approval; if you are denied access, you may be subject to reinvestigation of your existing Q or Top Secret clearance.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and related experience/training.
  • Core knowledge of analytic principles, procedures, methodologies, and intelligence-information dissemination.
  • Fundamental understanding of national-security issues related to the USIC.
  • Familiarity with classified and unclassified databases, software applications, and intelligence research tools used to identify and assess foreign capabilities.
  • Core training in areas such as espionage, counterproliferation, weapons systems, and/or foreign intelligence services.
  • Familiarity with hardware, software, and network-system fundamentals.
  • Ability to interpret and apply governmental and Laboratory policies, procedures, orders, and regulations.
  • Sufficient written, verbal, briefing, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to exercise tact, diplomacy, sound judgment, and discretion with highly sensitive information.

Additional qualifications at the K02.2 level

  • Related intelligence-field experience and applied knowledge of analytic principles, procedures, methodologies, and intelligence-information dissemination.
  • Knowledge and experience addressing national-security issues related to the USIC.
  • Experience using classified and unclassified databases, software applications, and intelligence research tools to identify and assess foreign capabilities using conventional intelligence disciplines.
  • Specialized training in espionage, counterproliferation, weapons systems, and/or foreign intelligence services.
  • Experience interpreting and applying governmental policies, procedures, orders, and regulations.
  • Strong written, verbal, briefing, and interpersonal communication skills.

Qualifications We Desire

  • Experience supporting CI/CT investigations, threat assessments, DOE data calls, or USIC coordination.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate complex analytical findings clearly in written products and briefings.

Pay Range

$95,820 - $117,312 Annually for the K02.1 level

$114,900 - $140,712 Annually for the K02.2 level

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting; pay will not be below any applicable local minimum wage. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Why Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory?

Pre-Employment Drug Test

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Please be aware of recruitment scams where people or entities are misusing the name of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) to post fake job advertisements. All current job openings are displayed on the Career Page under “Find Your Job” of our website. title: Shift Supervisor – Street Team
description:

ABOUT US

The Salvation Army is a Christian movement and one of Australia's largest and most-loved charities. We believe in doing good that transforms lives and futures for the better. It is this belief which drives us to find new ways and places where we can make a difference. From times of personal crisis to moments of national grief, we are always here — providing support, safety, community, and opportunity.

Shift Supervisor - Street Teams
Part Time | Hobart, TAS | SCHADS Level 4

Help Lead a Team Creating Safer Nights in Hobart

The Salvation Army is seeking a dedicated and community-focused Shift Supervisor to help lead our Street Team program operating within Hobart's Salamanca precinct.

Working closely with the Street Teams Team Leader, you'll coordinate volunteers and staff, support vulnerable and intoxicated patrons, and ensure the smooth operation of our late-night outreach service. This is an opportunity to combine leadership, community engagement and hands-on support to make a real difference in the lives of others.


About the Role

Street Teams operate every Friday and Saturday night in Hobart's Salamanca precinct, with occasional support provided at special events in Launceston.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Coordinating and supervising Street Team operations during shifts.
  • Supporting and guiding the Support Worker and volunteer teams.
  • Managing volunteer rosters and assisting with volunteer coordination.
  • Providing practical support and brief interventions to vulnerable patrons.
  • Liaising with Tasmania Police, Hobart City Council, Safer Nights Partnership, venue security and transport providers.
  • Managing resources and supplies, including the Street Team coffee cart.
  • Conducting shift debriefs and contributing to operational reporting.
  • Supporting risk management and promoting safe service delivery.

About You

You are approachable, reliable and passionate about helping people in vulnerable situations. You enjoy working as part of a team and can remain calm and professional in dynamic community settings.


Essential Requirements

  • Certificate IV in Alcohol and Other Drugs (AOD) or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Current National Police Check.
  • Current Working with Vulnerable People Registration.
  • Current Tasmanian Driver Licence.
  • Ability to tow and reverse a large trailer or van.
  • Current First Aid Certificate.
  • Willingness to complete mandatory Salvation Army training.

Highly Desirable

  • Mental Health First Aid Certificate.
  • Experience working with vulnerable individuals.
  • Experience in community services, outreach programs or volunteer-based environments.

Why Join Us?

The Salvos offer eligible employee's a well-balanced package of meaningful benefits including:

  • Salary packaging up to $15,900 tax free + $2,650 meal entertainment benefit.
  • Generous Paid Parental leave for primary (12 weeks) & secondary carers, Purchased Leave Scheme (up to 8 weeks) and 5 days paid leave per year to experience working in other TSA programs or activities.
  • Access to EAP and health & wellness initiatives incl Fitness Passport
  • Ongoing training and development opportunities that enhance on the job skills and proficiency.
  • Rewarding and fulfilling purpose driven careers that have positive and sustainable / social impacts.

How to Apply

If you are passionate about community outreach and ready to lead a team making a positive impact in Hobart, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and help make a difference in the lives of vulnerable Tasmanians.

The Salvation Army is an Equal Opportunity Employer who provides an inclusive work environment and embraces the diverse talent of its people. We value people of all cultures, languages, capacities, sexual orientations, gender identities and/or expressions. We are committed to achieving a diverse workforce and strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal people and Torres Strait Islander people.

The Salvation Army is a child safe organisation and is committed to protecting children and young people from harm. All child facing roles will require the successful completion of a Working with Children Check. Applicants for all roles require a mandatory Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check.

We value Integrity, Compassion, Respect, Diversity, and Collaboration

title: Casual Research Officer (Food Process Modelling and Consequential LCA)
description:
• Queensland Alliance for Agriculture and Food Innovation
  • Casual position with an hourly rate in the range of $64.28 to $68.96, plus superannuation of 12% (HEW Level 6).
  • Based at our St Lucia location



About This Opportunity

Join a collaborative research environment where you will help assess the environmental impacts of emerging food pathways. As the Research Officer, you will develop food process models and undertake consequential life cycle assessment (LCA), with a focus on sorghum foods such as flour, porridge and baked products.


Key responsibilities will include:


  • Develop and adapt process models in SuperPro Designer, including mass and energy balances, resource requirements, product recovery, losses and co-products.
  • Develop consequential LCA scenarios in SimaPro, considering system boundaries, supply, substitution and co-product effects.
  • Assess literature, supplier and project data, validate model outputs, and document key assumptions and uncertainties.
  • Analyse and communicate findings through sensitivity analysis, technical summaries and research outputs, and provide process inputs to the techno-economic assessment team.



About You

You will bring strong quantitative and analytical skills, with experience in process modelling, environmental assessment and technical data. You will ideally have:


  • A relevant degree in agriculture, chemical, biochemical, food process or environmental engineering, or a related quantitative discipline, with relevant experience.
  • Experience using process modelling software such as SuperPro Designer, including mass and energy balances and unit operations.
  • Experience using LCA software such as SimaPro to develop life cycle inventories and conduct LCA, including consequential modelling or substitution analysis.
  • Ability to assess system boundaries, marginal suppliers, co-product treatment, scale, yield and uncertainty assumptions.
  • Strong data management and analytical skills, including reproducible calculations and consistent management of units, datasets and model files.
  • Ability to evaluate technical evidence, solve modelling challenges and communicate findings clearly to researchers and industry collaborators.
  • Experience in cereal or food processing, Australian agricultural supply chains, industrial process data or model validation would be highly regarded.
  • Familiarity with technical reporting or publications, and R, Python or MATLAB would be advantageous.



About UQ

As part of the UQ community, you will have the opportunity to work alongside the brightest minds from around the world in an environment where interdisciplinary collaboration is encouraged. Working at UQ means joining an inclusive and connected community committed to creating positive change through research, education and community impact.



Interested?

For more information about this opportunity, please contact Associate Professor Sudhir Yadav, sudhir.yadav@uq.edu.au. For application inquiries, please reach out to the Talent Acquisition team at talent@uq.edu.au, stating the job reference number below in the subject line.


When you apply, please ensure you upload a resume and cover letter summarising how your background aligns to the ‘About You’ section. Please note that applications received via email will not be accepted.



Other Information

As a casual employee, and in line with Fair Work, please note that there is no commitment to ongoing work in this position.


Pre-employment checks may include: verification of the right to work in Australia, criminal history checks. This may also include checks relating to gender-based violence matters or other integrity and conduct requirements.


You must maintain unrestricted work rights in Australia for the duration of this appointment to apply. Employer sponsored work rights are not available for this appointment.

title: Pod Lead - Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering
description:
About Turing:
Turing is one of the world’s fastest-growing AI companies, accelerating the advancement and deployment of powerful AI systems.

Turing helps customers in two ways: Working with the world’s leading AI labs to advance frontier model capabilities in thinking, reasoning, coding, agentic behavior, multimodality, multilinguality, STEM and frontier knowledge; and leveraging that work to build real-world AI systems that solve mission-critical priorities for companies.

Role Overview:
  • We are seeking an experienced Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering expert to lead a team of technical trainers developing realistic, terminal-based engineering tasks for a frontier AI training and evaluation initiative.
  • In this role, you will oversee a pod of approximately 5–10 trainers, review engineering tasks for technical accuracy, reproducibility, and evaluation quality, and ensure that tasks reflect authentic mechanical and aerospace engineering workflows. You will also mentor trainers, maintain quality standards, and drive consistent task delivery.

What you'll do:
  • Lead and mentor a pod of technical trainers, ensuring consistent quality, productivity, and timely delivery of engineering tasks.
  • Review engineering tasks end to end, including problem statements, geometry and mesh files, simulation inputs, material properties, reference solutions, and automated tests.
  • Validate tasks involving finite-element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), thermodynamics, heat transfer, dynamics, robotics, flight simulation, propulsion, and orbital mechanics.
  • Ensure tasks reflect realistic mechanical and aerospace engineering workflows and require meaningful multi-step technical reasoning.
  • Verify engineering correctness across units, equilibrium, conservation laws, boundary conditions, mesh convergence, solver tolerances, reference frames, and numerical stability.
  • Validate computational environments, simulation tools, solvers, and dependencies to ensure reproducible results.
  • Review automated graders to ensure they evaluate meaningful engineering outputs such as stresses, deflections, natural frequencies, aerodynamic coefficients, thermal performance, orbital parameters, and safety margins.
  • Identify technical inaccuracies, unrealistic assumptions, incorrect tolerances, and opportunities to bypass engineering calculations or simulations.
  • Provide clear, actionable technical feedback, track revisions, and ensure quality issues are resolved before task approval.
  • Onboard trainers, allocate work, monitor quality and throughput, escalate blockers, and maintain technical documentation and best practices.

What we're looking for:
  • Ph.D., postdoctoral experience, or equivalent advanced technical experience in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
  • Strong programming skills in Python, C/C++, Fortran, Julia, or MATLAB/Octave, with proficiency in Linux environments.
  • Hands-on expertise in at least one major area: FEA, CFD, dynamics, flight simulation, thermal modeling, astrodynamics, guidance, navigation and control (GNC), or propulsion modeling.
  • Strong understanding of engineering simulation, numerical methods, computational modeling, and technical validation.
  • Experience reviewing complex technical work, engineering simulations, computational models, or research outputs.
  • Ability to evaluate engineering assumptions, numerical accuracy, solver convergence, and the reliability of computational results.
  • Strong analytical judgment with the ability to identify technical errors, edge cases, and flawed engineering assumptions.
  • Experience mentoring, reviewing, or leading small technical teams.
  • Excellent written communication skills for providing precise technical feedback and documenting quality standards.

Nice to have:
  • Experience with engineering simulation and computational tools such as OpenFOAM, SU2, CalculiX, Code_Aster, FEniCS, Elmer, Gmsh, FreeCAD, CadQuery, MuJoCo, ROS, XFOIL, AVL, OpenVSP, JSBSim, OpenMDAO, pyCycle, poliastro, Orekit, GMAT, or SPICE.
  • Familiarity with commercial engineering software such as ANSYS, Abaqus, COMSOL, or NASTRAN, including reproducing workflows using open-source tools.
  • Experience with state estimation, trajectory optimization, topology optimization, aeroelastic analysis, or multidisciplinary design optimization.
  • Familiarity with Docker, Git, CI/CD pipelines, and automated testing.
  • Experience developing or evaluating AI coding agents, terminal-based agents, or LLM-generated engineering solutions.
  • Industry or agency experience in automotive, energy, manufacturing, robotics, aircraft, launch vehicles, satellites, or UAVs.
  • Prior experience in AI training, technical quality control, benchmark development, or evaluation programs.

Offer Details:
  • Commitments Required: At least 4 hours per day and minimum 40 hours per week with overlap of 4 hours with PST.
  • Employment type : Contractor assignment (no medical/paid leave)
  • Duration of contract : 4 week [expected start date is next week]

title: Pod Lead - Life Science
description:
About Turing:
Turing is one of the world's leading AGI infrastructure companies, working with frontier AI labs to accelerate model development through high-quality training data, evaluations, and engineering talent.

Engagement Details:
  • Commitments Required: At least 6 hours per day and a minimum of 40 hours per week, with a 4-hour overlap with PST.
  • Employment Type: Contractor assignment (no medical/paid leave)
  • Duration of Contract: 5 weeks (expected start date is next week)

About the Role:
  • We are seeking an experienced Life Sciences or Medicine expert to lead a pod of trainers building realistic, terminal-based scientific and technical tasks for Terminal Bench Science. You will review every task your trainers produce for scientific correctness, reproducibility, data compliance, and grader reliability, and coach trainers to consistently deliver high-quality, challenging tasks.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Review trainer tasks end to end, including task statements, biological and clinical datasets, reference files, pipelines, environments, reference solutions, and automated tests.
  • Verify that tasks reflect authentic research or clinical analysis workflows and require genuine multi-step scientific reasoning.
  • Check that tools, reference genomes, annotation versions, databases, and dependencies are pinned and that pipelines are reproducible.
  • Validate scientific correctness, including genome builds, coordinate conventions, normalization, batch-effect handling, statistical assumptions, multiple-testing correction, units, dosing conventions, imaging orientation and spacing, and random-seed control.
  • Ensure graders verify substantive outputs such as variant calls, differential expression results, cluster assignments, binding or structural metrics, survival estimates, model performance, segmentation accuracy, and pharmacokinetic parameters rather than formatting.
  • Ensure tolerances account for legitimate stochastic and numerical variation without accepting incorrect analyses.
  • Ensure tasks cannot be gamed through hard-coded outputs, reading test files, or bypassing the intended analysis.
  • Confirm that all data is synthetic, public, appropriately licensed, and de-identified, with no protected health information or restricted-access data.
  • Screen tasks for biosafety and dual-use concerns.
  • Escalate content involving dangerous pathogens, toxins, or enhancement of harmful biological capabilities.
  • Provide clear, actionable written feedback and track revisions through closure.
  • Onboard and mentor trainers.
  • Allocate work, track quality and throughput, and escalate blockers.
  • Maintain pod documentation covering guidelines, recurring issues, and exemplary tasks.

title: Stagiair(e) Talent sourcing
company: Ministerie van Justitie en Veiligheid, Dienst Justitiële Inrichtingen
description:
Dit ga je doen

Ben jij sociaal, nieuwsgierig en vind je het leuk om nieuwe mensen te ontmoeten? Ben je benieuwd hoe je de juiste kandidaten vindt voor een organisatie als DJI? Wil je daarnaast jouw talenten inzetten voor een organisatie met maatschappelijke impact? Dan is deze meewerkstage iets voor jou!

Binnen Team Sourcing van de afdeling Werving & Selectie zoeken we vanaf januari of februari 2027 een enthousiaste stagiair(e) die ons team komt versterken. Tijdens deze stage ontdek je hoe online sourcing in de praktijk werkt, gaat actief op zoek naar potentiële kandidaten via verschillende online kanalen en leert hoe je hen op een effectieve manier benadert. We zijn landelijk actief en werken voor ongeveer 50 gevangenislocaties verspreid over Nederland. Tijdens de stage krijg je één of twee locaties of regio’s toegewezen waar sprake is van een bijzonder grote wervingsbehoefte. Je krijgt de mogelijkheid om veel praktijkervaring op te doen, jouw communicatieve vaardigheden verder te ontwikkelen en een kijkje te nemen achter de schermen van recruitment binnen de Dienst Justitiële Inrichtingen.

Team Sourcing is een snelgroeiend team binnen DJI en bestaat uit 17 enthousiaste collega’s. Binnen ons team houden we ons bezig met online sourcing, het actief zoeken en benaderen van potentiële kandidaten en het begeleiden van kandidaten gedurende het sollicitatieproces. Daarnaast organiseren we campagnes en evenementen om nieuw talent te bereiken. Wij richten ons op het vinden en enthousiasmeren van nieuwe collega’s voor executieve functies, zoals complexbeveiligers, penitentiair inrichtingswerkers (PIW), forensisch therapeutisch medewerkers en arbeidsbegeleiders.

Als Stagiair(e) Online Sourcer krijg je de kans om hier actief aan bij te dragen, leer je hoe je de juiste kandidaten vindt en ontdek je hoe je hen enthousiast maakt voor een baan bij DJI.

Wat ga je doen?
Tijdens deze meewerkstage draai je minimaal drie dagen per week mee binnen Team Sourcing, waarvan twee dagen op locatie en één dag in overleg. Je wordt onderdeel van het team en leert stap voor stap hoe het sourcingvak in de praktijk werkt.
Je houdt je onder andere bezig met:
• Het online zoeken naar geschikte kandidaten voor onze vacatures via platforms zoals LinkedIn en Indeed;
• Het actief benaderen en enthousiasmeren van potentiële kandidaten;
• Het opvolgen van kandidaten en onderhouden van contact;
• Het telefonisch contact leggen met kandidaten om hun interesse, wensen en mogelijkheden te bespreken;
• Het verwerken en opvolgen van leads uit evenementen en campagnes;
• Het meedenken over creatieve manieren om nieuwe kandidaten te bereiken.

Je krijgt goede begeleiding van ervaren collega's en volop de ruimte om jezelf te ontwikkelen. Zo leer je hoe je de juiste kandidaten vindt, hoe je contact met hen legt en hoe je hen enthousiast maakt voor een baan bij DJI. Geen dag is hetzelfde!

Dit bieden we nog meer

Duurt je stage langer dan een maand? Dan heb je recht op een stagevergoeding. Bij de Rijksoverheid geldt voor alle hbo- en wo-studenten een stagevergoeding van € 800,- bruto per maand bij een werkweek van 40 uur. Werk je minder dan 40 uur? Dan is je vergoeding naar rato. Naast je stagevergoeding heb je recht op betaalde vakantie-uren.

Meer informatie op P-Direkt

Dit vragen wij

Je ben enthousiast en krijgt energie van het leggen van nieuwe contacten. Je bent nieuwsgierig, durft initiatief te nemen en vindt het interessant om te ontdekken wat mensen beweegt in hun zoektocht naar een baan. Je hoeft nog geen ervaring te hebben met sourcing of recruitment. We vinden het vooral belangrijk dat je gemotiveerd bent om te leren en jezelf verder wilt ontwikkelen.

Daarnaast:
• Je volgt een hbo- of wo-opleiding, bij voorkeur in de richting van Human Resource Management, Commerciële Economie, Bedrijfskunde, Communicatie of een vergelijkbare studie;
• Je bent op zoek naar een meewerkstage en bent minimaal drie dagen per week beschikbaar;
• Je hebt interesse in recruitment, arbeidsmarktcommunicatie en online sourcing;
• Je bent communicatief vaardig en legt gemakkelijk telefonisch contact met kandidaten. Met jouw overtuigingskracht weet je ook latent werkzoekenden en twijfelaars enthousiast te maken en te motiveren om te solliciteren;
• Je bent nieuwsgierig, leergierig en neemt graag initiatief. Je werkt zelfstandig, maar krijgt ook energie van samenwerken binnen een enthousiast team.

Wat bieden we jou?
• Een stageplek waarin je veel leert over recruitment en sourcing;
• Begeleiding van ervaren professionals binnen Team Sourcing;
• De vrijheid om eigen ideeën en stageopdrachten uit te werken;
• Een warm welkom in een hecht en gedreven team;
• Een stagevergoeding van € 800,- per maand bij een werkweek van 40 uur. Loop je minder uren stage? Dan passen we de vergoeding naar rato aan.

Hier kom je te werken

Over Ministerie van Justitie en Veiligheid, Dienst Justitiële Inrichtingen

Werken bij de Rijksoverheid betekent een bijdrage leveren aan een beter Nederland. Dus ook aan een veilige en rechtvaardige samenleving voor iedereen. Justitie en Veiligheid verdedigt en beschermt de rechtsorde. Van beleid tot uitvoering.

Dienst Justitiële Inrichtingen

De Dienst Justitiële Inrichtingen (DJI) is niet alleen verantwoordelijk voor het uitvoeren van vrijheidsstraffen en vrijheidsbenemende maatregelen, maar ook voor de dagelijkse zorg van mensen die dit ondergaan. Dat zijn er jaarlijks meer dan 47.000. We bieden hun de kans om een maatschappelijk aanvaardbaar bestaan op te bouwen. Dat doen we met ruim 16.000 collega’s in gevangenissen, justitiële jeugdinrichtingen, forensisch psychiatrische centra en detentiecentra. Het is veelzijdig en boeiend werk. In alle gevallen houden we ons bezig met zaken die direct van invloed zijn op het dagelijks leven. Dat maakt werken voor DJI zo bijzonder. Want recht raakt mensen.

Ministerie van Justitie en Veiligheid, Dienst Justitiële Inrichtingen

Bijzonderheden

  • De standplaats is Den Haag. We zoeken een kandidaat die woonachtig is in Den Haag of omgeving, of die flexibel genoeg is om twee keer per week met het openbaar vervoer naar kantoor te reizen. Maandag is onze vaste kantoordag.
  • Op 24 en 25 november beoordelen wij de binnengekomen sollicitaties. Kandidaten die aansluiten bij het gewenste profiel, worden telefonisch benaderd. Op basis hiervan maken wij een verdere selectie voor de sollicitatiegesprekken. De sollicitatiegesprekken vinden plaats op 2 december 2026 op ons kantoor in Den Haag.
  • Vermeld in je motivatie waarom jij bij Team Sourcing wilt stagelopen en wat je graag wilt leren.
  • Om stage te lopen bij de Rijksoverheid, moet je een stageovereenkomst en geheimhoudingsverklaring ondertekenen en een Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag (VOG) overhandigen.

title: Biomedical Engineering Tech II
description:
Join the transformative team at City of Hope, where we're changing lives and making a real difference in the fight against cancer, diabetes, and other life-threatening illnesses. City of Hope’s growing national system includes its Los Angeles campus, a network of clinical care locations across Southern California, a new cancer center in Orange County, California, and treatment facilities in Atlanta, Chicago and Phoenix. Our dedicated and compassionate employees are driven by a common mission\: To deliver the cures of tomorrow to the people who need them today.

** Typical work schedule is 10\:00 am - 7\:00 pm Monday through Friday. Weekend coverage availability is required**

Position Summary

Bring your biomedical equipment expertise to a mission-driven healthcare environment where reliable technology directly supports exceptional patient care. As a Biomedical Engineering Technician II (BMET II), you will inspect, calibrate, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair a broad range of medical devices used across clinical settings. You will partner closely with clinical teams, biomedical engineering, IT, vendors, and other key stakeholders to help ensure medical equipment is safe, reliable, compliant, and ready when patients and caregivers need it most.

As a successful candidate, you will\:

  • Perform preventive maintenance, inspections, and repairs on medical equipment including patient monitors, infusion pumps, defibrillators, ventilators, and other biomedical devices.
  • Troubleshoot complex equipment issues using diagnostic software, service manuals, schematics, and electronic testing equipment.
  • Calibrate medical devices according to manufacturer specifications to help ensure accurate and safe operation.
  • Respond to equipment issues reported by clinical teams and provide timely solutions that minimize equipment downtime.
  • Support the installation, configuration, inspection, acceptance testing, and deployment of new medical devices.
  • Maintain accurate equipment inventory, repair, service, performance-check, warranty, and location information using the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).
  • Provide technical support and training to clinical staff on the proper use and basic maintenance of medical equipment.
  • Collaborate with vendors and manufacturers to resolve technical issues and support equipment covered under warranty.
  • Ensure work complies with applicable regulatory requirements and standards, including those established by The Joint Commission and FDA, and participate in safety audits and risk assessments when required.

title: #DIGITAL CAMPUS - Observability IT operation specialist
description:
Job Description:

#DIGITAL CAMPUS - End to end monitoring support


An opportunity for an End to end monitoring support has arisen within Airbus Helicopters (Albacete, Spain)


WHY JOIN US?

📍 LIFE IN ALBACETE: QUALITY & CONVENIENCE -

Albacete is a dynamic, historic city in Spain, located in the region of Castilla-La Mancha. This modern urban center, known for its rich cultural heritage, and it is conveniently close to Madrid and the Mediterranean coast.

Forget long commutes. Albacete offers you the great advantage of a “15-minute city": safe, accessible, comfortable and perfectly connected. Enjoy a premium standard of living at a competitive cost, ensuring you have the perfect balance between your career and your personal life.

🚁 AIRBUS HELICOPTERS: GROW WITH US - We offer more than a job; we offer a community. Immerse yourself in a young, collaborative environment that feels like family. As a strategic Center of Excellence, we are a global leader in helicopter production, offering you endless potential to grow alongside our major projects.

✨THE PROJECT: SHAPING THE FUTURE - Welcome to the Digital Campus, a pioneering ecosystem dedicated to industrial digitalization and innovation. This is more than just a workplace; it is a technological hub where we define the future of flight.

Bring your ideas to a dynamic, modern ecosystem and help us build the next generation of aerospace solutions.


DESCRIPTION


  • Your main missions are focused on leveraging the integration of the observability tools in the Airbus Helicopters digital landscape and to optimize their usage. You will manage the automation of our testing and observability ecosystems. In this role, you will eliminate manual operational toil, ensure that our systems are highly observable, and build a robust, automated testing pipeline that accelerates our deployment velocity without compromising stability.
    You will bridge the gap between development, testers, and operations by automating our existing workflows, standardizing our observability stack, and taking a hands-on approach to deploying test automation infrastructure.



YOUR CHALLENGES

- Automation of Existing Operations

    • Modernize & Automate: Take full ownership of our current operational baseline by identifying and automating existing manual or semi-manual processe
    • Deployment as Code: Transition legacy deployment strategies into fully codified, automated "Deployment as Code" pipelines.
    • Configuration Management: Streamline, maintain, and expand our automated operational tasks (e.g., standardizing and scheduling Ansible jobs, cron jobs, and maintenance scripts).

- Observability & Monitoring Automation

    • OpenTelemetry (Otel) Deployment: Take the lead on designing, deploying, and maintaining OpenTelemetry across our entire infrastructure to standardize the collection and routing of traces, metrics, and logs.
    • Extensions Development: Design, write, and maintain custom plugins, exporters, and extensions for our observability ecosystem. You will build tailored monitoring solutions to extract deep telemetry data from proprietary applications, legacy systems, and niche infrastructure that out-of-the-box tools cannot reach.

- Test Automation Infrastructure

    • Test Automation Deployment: Take a direct, hands-on role in deploying, configuring, and scaling the testing frameworks and automation tools utilized by the software teams.

SKILLS

  • Master's degree level (or equivalent) in Information Technology or related field
  • Experience with observability tools (monitoring, testing, alerting, open telemetry) is a plus
  • General knowledge on IT infrastructure (network, technical infrastructure) and ITIL concepts
  • Knowledge in scripting languages to develop automation (Python, Java, Custom API integration)
  • Automation & Scripting: Strong proficiency in configuration management and automation tools, specifically Ansible.
  • Deployment as code
  • Proficiency in creating and managing technical documentation
  • Proven production environment management; strong troubleshooting skills
  • Curious, open-minded, collaborative team player with strong communication skills
  • Autonomous, organized, delivery/customer-oriented, technology enthusiast and crisis facing robustness
  • Experience working on projects with international teams and stakeholders
  • Fluent English

WHICH BENEFITS WILL YOU HAVE AS AIRBUS EMPLOYEE?

At Airbus we are focused on our employees and their welfare. Take a look at some of our social benefits:

  • Vacation days plus additional days-off along the year (Apróx. 35 days per year in total).

title: PRU017U
description:
This is a remote/ rotational position, working two weeks on and two weeks off or three weeks on and three weeks off, in Prudhoe Bay, AK. The typical schedule is 84 hours per week (40 hours straight time and a minimum of 44 hours at time and a half). All meals and lodging are provided by Worley while the employee is on location. Transportation between Anchorage and Prudhoe Bay is provided.

Worley offers a competitive benefits package, with company paid short-term disability, life insurance, paid sick leave, and 4.5% employer match on 401k.

Job Purpose\:

Install new electrical systems, equipment, wiring and controls in an existing brown field petrochemical environment.

Essential Job Functions\:

  • Assists Electrical Journeyman in setup and performance of job tasks.

  • Assist Journeyman with maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, installation and construction of industrial electrical equipment and systems found in an industrial environment through the proper use of standard wire, conduit, cable tray, fittings and hardware commonly found in industrial plants.

  • Assist Journeyman while learning to bend, cut, thread, and install conduit.

  • Assist in pulling MC-HL cable and installation.

  • Help Journeyman install and terminate wiring.

  • Learn applicable NEC codes that pertain to all installations performed.

  • Responsible for use and care for the tools and equipment commonly employed in industrial construction such as hydraulic/electric benders, knockout punch sets, cable puller, meggers, hi-pot equipment, volt meters, multi-testers and amp-meters and other electrical parts.

  • Assist other crafts with general labor work.

  • Participate in daily and weekly Toolbox meeting.

  • Must be able to follow all company, client, safety, and regulatory requirements, including, but not limited to, policies, procedures, standards, and guidelines as they relate to this position and the work duties being performed.

  • Have adequate written and oral communications applicable to standards set by organization.

  • Complete all ABC apprentice testing requirements.

  • Routinely operate Worley/client light and/or medium duty vehicles.

  • Safely climb ladders of various heights.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities\:

  • Possesses current knowledge of Apprentice Electrician, have physical fitness card and an understanding of organizational practices.

  • Basic understanding of electrical circuits including the operation and function of typical electrical devices and machinery such as solenoids, relays, motors, transformers, switches, motor control centers, generators, batteries, and lighting systems.

  • Possess an excellent knowledge of the National Electric Code.

  • Adequate written and oral communications applicable to standards set by organization.

  • Ability to interpret electrical drawings and schematics.

  • Proficient in NFPA70E.

Physical Demands/Work Environment\:
Work is performed in a remote Arctic environment with limited medical resources. Candidate understands the site is approximately 840 miles (at least 4 hours by air ambulance) from surgical, specialist, and tertiary medical care, and where medical evacuation from this location may be significantly delayed due to weather conditions. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the essential functions of this job, the employee is required to\:

  • Must have ability to stand, walk on level, uneven and slippery surfaces, sit, squat, kneel, crawl, reach through low and high ranges, work overhead, and exhibit normal balance and coordination. These basic physical requirements are essential for safe performance of the job in harsh environments with exposure to very cold temperatures and while wearing arctic gear.

  • Standing for prolonged periods of time.

  • Driving for prolonged periods of time in the dark and inclement weather

  • Ability to climb scaffold, ramps, stairs, equipment, portable ladders, and/or wellhouse/tank/facility fixed ladders of 20 feet or greater.

  • Ability to wear and utilize fall protection within manufacturer specifications.

  • Lift 50 lbs. from floor to waist with two hands.

  • Lift 50 lbs. from floor to shoulder with two hands.

  • Carry 50 lbs. for 15 feet with two hands.

  • Push/pull 60 lbs. sled for 20 feet.

  • Push/pull 90 lbs. cart for 20 feet.

This job description is intended to describe the nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this position. It is not to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities and duties required of the job incumbents. Worley provides reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities, including both applicants and employees, to allow the individual to perform the essential functions of the job, unless doing so would create an undue hardship.

In-Vehicle Monitoring System\: As part of our commitment to safety and accountability, company vehicles are equipped with in-cab cameras and vehicle monitoring systems. These systems may record video and audio, as well as collect GPS location, vehicle speed, harsh braking, rapid acceleration and other driving behaviors. All data is subject to review by management to ensure compliance with company policies and safe driving practices.

title: Senior Scheduling Coordinator
description:
Number of Positions Available:

1

ABOUT US

The Salvation Army is a Christian movement and one of Australia's largest and most-loved charities. We believe in doing good that transforms lives and futures for the better. It is this belief which drives us to find new ways and places where we can make a difference. From times of personal crisis to moments of national grief, we are always here — providing support, safety, community, and opportunity.

Senior Scheduling Coordinator – Residential Aged Care

  • Permanent full-time
  • Hybrid working
  • Based in Riverview, Brisbane

This is scheduling at scale


Nineteen residential aged-care services. Seven states and territories. Approximately 2,200 permanent and casual employees. Multiple awards and at least four enterprise agreements.


Our scheduling team coordinates the workforce that keeps these services operating around the clock, including Registered Nurses, Enrolled Nurses, Care Service Employees and Lifestyle staff. The team also manages agency and temporary workforce requirements, while catering and housekeeping services are outsourced.


Behind those numbers are residents who depend on having the right people, with the right skills, in the right place—every shift, every day.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Scheduling Coordinator who can step into this environment, take ownership and make an immediate contribution.



The team you’ll join


You will work alongside six Scheduling Coordinators, most of whom are based together at Riverview, with one team member working remotely. As such we are open to candidates based in Brisbane only.

You will report to an experienced Scheduling Manager who knows the function, the team and the operational environment. This role has no formal direct reports, but it carries genuine operational leadership responsibility.

You will be expected to provide guidance and mentorship, coordinate priorities and support the team when challenges arise. You will also help set expectations, follow up agreed actions and ensure people remain accountable for delivering accurate, timely and compliant scheduling outcomes.


The role we need you to play


We are not looking for someone who needs to learn scheduling from the beginning. We need an experienced operator who can understand an established function quickly, work confidently within complex workforce arrangements and become a trusted point of escalation for the team.


What success will look like


You will earn the confidence of the scheduling team without taking over their work. You will provide support when it is needed, ask the right questions and follow through when expectations are not being met.

You will be comfortable making decisions, escalating risk and constructively challenging stakeholders. You will understand that a roster is not simply a schedule—it affects resident care, employee wellbeing, regulatory compliance, payroll accuracy and workforce cost.


What you’ll bring

  • Strong recent experience in a complex, high-volume scheduling or rostering environment.
  • Experience within residential aged care, healthcare or another 24/7 regulated service.
  • A practical understanding of Care Minutes and mandatory 24/7 Registered Nurse coverage.
  • Experience working across multiple awards, enterprise agreements and employee types.
  • Strong knowledge of UKG, Kronos or another sophisticated workforce management platform.
  • Experience with Workday and Emprevo would be advantageous.
  • The ability to analyse workforce information and identify roster, compliance and cost risks.
  • Confidence coaching colleagues, coordinating work and addressing gaps in performance.
  • Strong stakeholder skills and the judgement to know when to resolve, challenge or escalate an issue.
  • Intermediate to advanced Excel and workforce reporting capability.
  • A Diploma-level qualification in business, commerce, administration or a related discipline.

What we offer

  • A senior role with genuine influence across a national scheduling function.
  • An experienced manager and established team to work alongside.
  • The opportunity to contribute your knowledge and introduce better ways of working.
  • Hybrid and flexible working arrangements.
  • Salary packaging of up to $15,900 each year, plus up to $2,650 for meals and entertainment.
  • Up to 12 weeks’ paid parental leave.
  • Novated vehicle leasing.
  • Access to a comprehensive Employee Assistance Program.

If you are an experienced scheduling professional who can bring sound judgement, ownership and calm leadership to a complex national workforce, we would like to hear from you.

The Salvation Army is an Equal Opportunity Employer who provides an inclusive work environment and embraces the diverse talent of its people. We value people of all cultures, languages, capacities, sexual orientations, gender identities and/or expressions. We are committed to achieving a diverse workforce and strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal people and Torres Strait Islander people.

The Salvation Army is a child safe organisation and is committed to protecting children and young people from harm. All child facing roles will require the successful completion of a Working with Children Check. Applicants for all roles require a mandatory Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check.

We value Integrity, Compassion, Respect, Diversity, and Collaboration

title: Executive Coordinator - Office of the Provost
description:
Overview:


  • Work directly with RMIT’s incoming Provost in a highly trusted executive support role.
  • Bring your judgement, organisation and stakeholder skills to the heart of RMIT’s academic leadership.
  • Continuing, full-time HEW 7, Melbourne City campus.



About the role


This is an opportunity to work directly with RMIT’s incoming Provost and play an important role in establishing and operating the Office of the Provost.

As Executive Coordinator, you will provide high level executive, administrative, and coordination support across a complex portfolio. You will be a trusted point of coordination, helping the Provost manage priorities, information, meetings, and actions, while anticipating requirements and ensuring important matters are progressed and followed through.

Working with senior stakeholders across RMIT, you will exercise sound judgement and discretion, manage competing priorities, and help ensure the Provost’s time and attention are directed to the matters that require them most.


What you will do


  • Provide high level executive support to the Provost, including complex diary, meeting, correspondence, and communication management.
  • Coordinate the Provost’s forward schedule and priorities, anticipating upcoming commitments, dependencies, and information requirements.
  • Coordinate briefings, presentations, meeting papers, reports, and other information to ensure the Provost is well prepared for key engagements and decisions.
  • Triage requests and incoming matters, using sound judgement to prioritise, redirect, or escalate issues, protect the Provost’s time, and ensure attention is directed to the matters requiring it most.
  • Provide secretariat and coordination support for committees, working groups, and meetings, including tracking actions and ensuring timely follow through.
  • Build strong relationships across RMIT and act as an effective point of connection between the Provost’s Office and senior internal and external stakeholders.
  • Support projects, events, travel, office systems, records, and financial administration, contributing to the smooth day to day operation of the Provost’s Office.

What will help you succeed


You will be an accomplished executive support professional who is comfortable working with a high degree of autonomy in a large and complex organisation.


You will bring:


  • significant experience supporting a senior executive, with demonstrated discretion, judgement, and professionalism
  • exceptional organisational skills and the ability to anticipate needs, manage competing priorities, and remain calm when circumstances change
  • excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing high quality correspondence, briefings, and executive materials
  • confidence working with senior stakeholders and building trusted relationships across a complex organisation
  • strong problem solving skills and the confidence to appropriately question, clarify, and escalate issues when required
  • an ability to look ahead, identify emerging requirements, and ensure that commitments, information, and actions are managed effectively
  • experience supporting governance, committees, projects, and administrative processes, together with strong capability across Microsoft 365.

Experience within a university or similarly complex organisation will be highly regarded, as will an understanding of the Australian higher education environment.


Why join RMIT?


The Executive Coordinator will join RMIT at an exciting time, supporting the incoming Provost as they establish their office and build relationships across the University.

This is an opportunity to become a trusted partner to one of RMIT’s most senior leaders and contribute to an office that connects across the academic and professional community.

For someone who enjoys being at the centre of a complex organisation, making things happen behind the scenes and enabling an executive to operate at their best, this is a role with significant visibility, variety and impact.
